strings.{actor} 一把掀开石磊的工作服：怀里揣着一个铝饭盒，盖子上刻着一个“郝”字: {actor} throws open Larry Shi's work jacket: an aluminium lunch tin against his chest, the lid carved with “Hao”.
strings.{actor} 借着灯写了很久，写完又划掉，划掉又写。: {actor} writes by lamplight for a long time: writes, crosses out, writes again.
strings.{actor} 冲他摇了摇头，指了指他的口袋。小满赶紧把手机关了，塞回了夹层里。: {actor} shakes {actor.his} head at him and points at his pocket. Manny switches the phone off fast and shoves it back into the lining.
strings.{actor} 和旁边的人聊起了出事以前的日子。: {actor} talks with the man beside {actor.him} about the days before it happened.
strings.{actor} 和石磊做了交易：一口饭，换一句不说。: {actor} strikes a deal with Larry Shi: a mouthful of food for one thing not said.
strings.{actor} 哼起了《走西口》，黑暗里有几个人也跟着哼了起来。: {actor} hums “Zou Xikou”, and in the dark a few others hum along.
strings.{actor} 在水边待久了，眼前一阵阵发黑，头疼欲裂——坡底的二氧化碳太浓了。: {actor} stays too long at the water's edge; the world keeps going black and {actor.his} head feels ready to split—the carbon dioxide at the bottom of the slope is too thick.
strings.{actor} 在水边的烂泥里滑了一跤，整个人栽进水里，被绳子拽了回来。: {actor} slips in the mud at the water's edge, goes headfirst into the water and is hauled back on the rope.
strings.{actor} 在纸条上写：“井下还有一个人，叫韦德贵，贵州人，外包队的。请告诉: {actor} writes on the slip of paper: “There's another man down here—Doug Wei, from Guizhou, contract crew. Please tell his family.”
strings.{actor} 帮田立新拧干湿透的工作服时，从他内衣口袋里摸出一个塑封的小本子—: {actor} is wringing out Leon Tian's soaked work jacket when {actor.he} feels a small laminated notebook in the inside pocket—the hazard inspection log. The newest page has been torn out, and on the ragged edge left behind the words “water at the 1203 face” can still be made out.
strings.{actor} 想起了家里的人。: {actor} thinks of the people at home.
strings.{actor} 扑了个空，老鼠钻回了缝里。: {actor} grabs at nothing; the rat is back in its crack.
strings.{actor} 打着灯在水边来回照了很久。水面平平的，什么也没有。: {actor} sweeps the lamp back and forth along the water's edge for a long time. The surface is flat. Nothing.
strings.{actor} 打着灯，顺着老鼠钻进去的那道缝一点点往里摸。: {actor} holds the lamp up and feels {actor.his} way in, inch by inch, along the crack the rat went through.
strings.{actor} 把一张纸嚼成了浆，慢慢咽了下去。: {actor} chews a sheet of paper to pulp and swallows it slowly.
strings.{actor} 把信贴在胸口，读了一遍又一遍。: {actor} presses the letter to {actor.his} chest and reads it over and over.
strings.{actor} 把本子举到了矿灯底下。: {actor} holds the notebook up under the cap lamp.
strings.{actor} 把本子塞回了田立新手里。田立新愣了一下，低声说了句谢谢。: {actor} shoves the notebook back into Leon Tian's hand. Leon Tian freezes, then says thank you, quietly.
strings.{actor} 把田立新的记录本藏进了自己的口袋。: {actor} hides Leon Tian's notebook in {actor.his} own pocket.
strings.{actor} 把皮带泡软了，一点点啃下一截。又苦又涩。: {actor} soaks {actor.his} belt soft and gnaws off a length of it. Bitter, and it puckers the mouth.
strings.{actor} 把耳朵贴在管子上：很远很远的地方，好像有人在回敲。: {actor} presses an ear to the pipe: far, far away, it sounds like someone knocking back.
strings.{actor} 把自己的那块饼干掰下一大半，塞进了小满手里。: {actor} breaks off most of {actor.his} biscuit and presses it into Manny's hand.
strings.{actor} 把身子蜷起来，用膝盖压住了胃。: {actor} curls up and presses {actor.his} knees into {actor.his} stomach.
strings.{actor} 把那双胶靴并排摆在木板底下，烟盒纸叠好，塞进了自己的口袋。: {actor} sets the rubber boots side by side under the plank, folds the cigarette-packet paper and slips it into {actor.his} pocket.
strings.{actor} 抡起镐把，一下一下地敲：三长两短。: {actor} swings the pick handle and knocks, again and again: three long, two short.
strings.{actor} 拎着镐，带着小满在坑木上刮了半宿。小满学得快，嚼着嚼着就靠着煤帮: {actor} carries the pick and scrapes at the pit props with Manny half the night. Manny learns fast; chewing, chewing, he falls asleep against the coal wall.
strings.{actor} 挑了一块亮晶晶的精煤含在嘴里，嚼得咯吱咯吱响。没有味道，可嘴里有: {actor} picks out a shiny lump of clean coal and holds it in {actor.his} mouth, crunching it. No taste at all, but with something in {actor.his} mouth the stomach stops knotting so hard.
strings.{actor} 没入黑水以后，再也没有浮上来。大家对着水面喊了一夜。: {actor} goes under the black water and never comes back up. They call across the water all night.
strings.{actor} 深吸了几口气，没入了黑水。所有人盯着水面，数着自己的心跳……过了: {actor} takes a few deep breaths and slips under the black water. Everyone stares at the surface, counting their own heartbeats… After a long, long time, faint knocking comes from the far end of the slope: three long, two short—{actor.he} made it!
strings.{actor} 用钢钎在砖缝里凿出一个拳头大的洞，把水壶塞了过去。那边的人咕咚咕: {actor} works a fist-sized hole through the brickwork with a steel bar and pushes the water bottle through. On the other side the man drinks it down in gulps, thanks {actor.him} in a hoarse voice and says: “My name is Charlie Zhao.”
strings.{actor} 的矿灯照见一只大个的老鼠——不是灰子——从煤帮的缝里钻了出来，嗅: {actor}'s cap lamp catches a big rat—not Smoky—sliding out of a crack in the coal wall. It sniffs, and shrinks back in.
strings.{actor} 看见小满缩在角落里，用身子挡着一点亮光——他从工作服夹层里摸出了: {actor} sees Manny hunched in a corner, his body shielding a little light—he has fished an old phone out of the lining of his work jacket. Phones are strictly banned underground; he has kept it hidden all along, and two bars of charge are left. The lock screen is a photo: a skinny half-grown boy grinning at a cake, with two numeral candles stuck in it, a “1” and a “7”.
strings.{actor} 突然发起了高烧，浑身的肌肉疼得碰都不敢碰，眼睛也红了。王福山看了: {actor} comes down with a sudden high fever; every muscle aches so badly that no one dares touch {actor.him}, and {actor.his} eyes are red. Felix Wang takes one look and his face changes: “It's a disease off the rats.”
strings.{actor} 翻了个身，假装睡着了。: {actor} rolls over and pretends to be asleep.
strings.{actor} 翻了个身，用胳膊捂住了耳朵。: {actor} rolls over and covers {actor.his} ears with an arm.
strings.{actor} 被乔卫东绑在身上，没入了黑水。一个多钟头后，管子里传来约好的三声: {actor} is strapped to Wayne Qiao and goes under the black water. A little over an hour later, the agreed three knocks come along the pipe: {actor.he} made it.
strings.{actor} 被赶到了坡下的水边，一个人，没有灯。: {actor} is driven down to the water's edge at the bottom of the slope—alone, no lamp.
strings.{actor} 裹着湿衣服，一口一口地灌水。: {actor} sits in soaked clothes, gulping water mouthful by mouthful.
strings.{actor} 逮住了它。生的，可谁也没嫌弃。: {actor} catches it. Raw—but nobody turns their nose up.
strings.{target} 抱着饭盒游了回来，冻得嘴唇发紫，咧着嘴笑。: {target} swims back with the lunch tin clutched to {target.his} chest, lips purple with cold, grinning.
strings.{target} 游到一半呛了好几口黑水，被拽了回来。饭盒漂走了。: {target} chokes on mouthfuls of black water halfway across and is hauled back. The lunch tin drifts away.
strings.{target} 脱掉工作服，腰上拴着一根风筒布条，咬着牙下了水。: {target} strips off {target.his} work jacket, a strip of duct cloth tied round {target.his} waist, and goes into the water with {target.his} teeth clenched.
strings.“咔嚓”一声，一根被压断的棚梁砸了下来，煤和矸石哗啦啦塌了一片——有人被压在了下: With a crack, a snapped roof beam comes down and a whole stretch of coal and rock collapses—someone is pinned underneath! The roof is still shedding.
strings.“哐——”头顶的岩层里一声巨响，煤渣哗哗往下掉，一截钻杆从顶板里捅了出来，停在离: Bang—a huge noise in the rock overhead, coal grit raining down, and a length of drill rod punches through the roof and stops less than ten metres from the platform! Someone up there is knocking on the rod: thud, thud, thud. They've found you. The rod goes back up any moment—what do you write on the first slip of paper you tie to it?
strings.“说什么胡话。”那份吃的，又塞回了他手里。: “What nonsense.” The food is pushed back into his hand.
strings.一下、两下……{aliveCount} 下。管子那头沉默了一会儿，也回了 {al: One, two… {aliveCount}. The pipe is silent for a moment, then knocks back {aliveCount}.
strings.一个泡了水的急救包，里面的纱布还能用: A waterlogged first-aid pouch; the gauze inside is still usable
strings.一个漂过来的饭盒，盖子扣得很紧，里面的饭只湿了一角: A lunch tin that floated over, its lid jammed tight, the rice only wet in one corner
strings.一卷废电缆和半截风筒布，正好拿来搓绳子: A coil of scrap cable and half a length of duct cloth—just the thing for twisting rope
strings.一口贵州腔，爱说“要得”“晓得了”，叫人都带“叔”“哥”；说着说着，声音就变回了: A thick Guizhou accent; fond of “All right” and “Got it”; calls everyone “Uncle” or “Brother”. The longer he talks, the more he sounds like a little boy.
strings.一只灰毛老鼠，尾巴尖秃了一截，不知在这条上山里住了多久，平时就靠矿工饭盒里掉的渣: A grey rat with the tip of its tail gone bald. Nobody knows how long it has lived in this rise, getting by on the crumbs that fall from the miners' lunch tins. The day the water broke in, it was up the slope before any of the men. The mine has an old rule: you don't kill rats underground. The old-timers say that where there are rats there's air to breathe, and when the rats bolt in a panic, the roof or the water is about to come.
strings.一小簇火苗舔着树皮，烤焦的味道在巷道里散开。谁也没说话，只是盯着那点光。: A small flame licks at the bark, and the smell of scorching spreads down the roadway. Nobody speaks; they just stare at the light.
strings.一整天过去了，坡下的水面一点也没降，在矿灯下纹丝不动。有人说：是不是地面的水泵停: A whole day gone, and the water below the slope has not dropped at all; in the lamplight it is dead still. Someone says: have the pumps on the surface stopped?
strings.一根粗细不匀、疙疙瘩瘩的绳子盘在了平台上，每隔一米打了一个结。: A lumpy rope of uneven thickness lies coiled on the platform, a knot tied every metre.
strings.一点点热量；鞣过的皮子可能让人中毒: A little warmth; tanned hide can poison you
strings.一点肉（约 150 千卡）；井下的老鼠可能带病，老矿工们心里也会发毛: A little meat (about 150 kcal); rats underground can carry disease, and even old miners get the shivers
strings.一点肉；可井下的老鼠可能带病: A little meat; but rats underground can carry disease
strings.一盏挂在钢丝上的矿灯，电池还有电: A cap lamp caught on a wire rope, battery still holding some charge
strings.一遍遍敲管子，告诉上面：下面还有人: Knock the pipe again and again, tell them up top: there are still men down here
strings.一道蓝白色的火光贴着顶板横扫过去，紧接着是一声把人五脏六腑都震错了位的闷响——瓦: A blue-white flash of flame sweeps along the roof, then a dull roar that knocks a man's guts out of place—a methane explosion.
strings.一顶漂着的安全帽，帽圈上写着别人的名字: A floating hard hat with someone else's name written inside the band
strings.三个人把他死死抱住，一直等到他不再发抖。: Three men hold him fast until the shaking stops.
strings.三个饭盒（米饭、土豆丝、几片肥肉）、半袋饼干和小满揣着的两包方便面。后来刮下的树: Three lunch tins (rice, shredded potato, a few slices of fatty pork), half a bag of biscuits and the two packs of instant noodles Manny had on him. Later this also counts the inner bark you scrape off, whatever you fish out of the water and the nutrient drinks sent down the borehole.
strings.三天前你在 1203 面就查出了透水征兆——迎头出水、有一股臭鸡蛋味，按规定必须: Three days ago you found the warning signs at the 1203 face: water seeping at the head, a smell of rotten eggs. The rules required production to stop for exploratory drainage. You wrote it into the hazard inspection log—but the mine manager had you tear out the page and rewrite it as “no anomalies”, and pressed two thousand yuan into your hand. You took it. You know everything the mine has covered up, and you're part of it.
strings.三月底，山西某县福源煤业，3 号煤层 1203 掘进工作面。下午两点二十，迎头一: Late March, Fuyuan Coal, a mine in a county in Shanxi: the 1203 development heading in the No. 3 seam. At twenty past two in the afternoon, just after a round of shots had been fired at the face, a muffled roar like thunder came from inside the coal—they had blasted into the old workings. Black water, pent up for who knows how many years, burst out with lumps of coal and timber in it, and within minutes the haulage road was full.
strings.上头的水泵加到了十二台，一天能降一米多。再撑两天。: They've got twelve pumps running up top now. It'll drop more than a metre a day. Two more days.
strings.不会说话，只有吱吱声和爪子挠煤的窸窣声。: It can't talk—only squeaks, and the scratch of claws on coal.
strings.不动——密闭一开，所有人都可能搭进去: Don't touch it—open the seal and everyone could go with it
strings.不动急救包，拿坑木条和皮带固定: Don't use the first-aid kit; splint the leg with a strip of pit prop and a belt
strings.不给它吃的，也不打它: Don't feed it, don't hit it
strings.不行，一人一份，谁也不能少: No. One share each. Nobody gets less
strings.不让墙里的气涌出来，先看看他还撑不撑得住；要用掉 1.5 升水: Don't let the gas behind the wall pour out; first see if he can hold on. Costs 1.5 L of water
strings.两个人先抬起一根坑木顶住了顶板，这才开始刨人。被压的人一直在叫，后来就不叫了。: Two men lift a pit prop and jam it against the roof before they start digging. The pinned man keeps calling out; then he stops calling.
strings.两个人扯着风筒布，一下一下地往下扇，扇到胳膊都抬不起来。: Two men work the duct cloth, fanning down, stroke after stroke, until their arms won't lift.
strings.两台自救器在黑暗里一个一个传下去，每人吸上几口。: Two self-rescuers pass from hand to hand in the dark; everyone takes a few breaths.
strings.两盏灯一直亮着，照着每个人的脸。至少，能看清彼此还在。: Two lamps stay lit, lighting every face. At least you can see one another, still there.
strings.乔卫东咬上咬嘴，顺着导向绳没入了黑水。: Wayne Qiao bites down on the mouthpiece and follows the guide rope into the black water.
strings.乔卫东把每个人的伤情、还剩几盏灯、水面离平台多高，一条条记在防水板上。临走前他说: Wayne Qiao writes it all on the waterproof board, line by line: each man's injuries, how many lamps are left, how far the water sits below the platform. Before he goes he says: “Three days, at most.”
strings.乔卫东把气瓶靠在煤帮上，先挨个看了伤员，又抬手敲了敲顶板：“这根棚子吃劲了。递根: Wayne Qiao leans his tank against the coal wall, checks the injured one by one, then raps the roof with his knuckles: “This prop's taking the load. Pass me a piece of timber.”
strings.乔卫东是跟着最后一趟橡皮艇出来的。上了井口，他把面罩往脖子上一挂，蹲在地上抽了半: Wayne Qiao came out on the last rubber boat. At the pithead he hung his mask round his neck, squatted on the ground, smoked half a cigarette and said nothing. The next year he started mine-diving training in the rescue corps. Before that, he had been the only one in the province who could do it.
strings.乔卫东是那次救援里唯一牺牲的救护队员。他的气瓶后来摆进了救护大队的荣誉室，瓶身上: Wayne Qiao was the only rescuer who died in that rescue. His air tank stands in the rescue corps' hall of honour, his name painted on it in red. On their first day of dive training, every new recruit stands in front of that tank for a while.
strings.乔卫东潜回去以后，在那条大巷里又下了十一次水。那年他拿了一枚救援奖章，挂在家里挂: After he dived back out, Wayne Qiao went into the water of that main roadway eleven more times. That year he was given a rescue medal, which hangs at home on the nail that holds the calendar. He says what he remembers most isn't the water; it's the faces in that rise, gaunt and lit up one by one by his lamp.
strings.乔卫东给贺小勇扣上备用面罩，用两根带子把他和自己绑在一起：“别憋气，正常喘。抓住: Wayne Qiao fits the spare mask over Eddie Ho's face and straps him to himself with two webbing straps: “Don't hold your breath, breathe normally. Grab my belt and don't let go, whatever you touch.”
strings.乔卫东给那人扣上备用面罩，用两根带子把他和自己绑在一起：“别憋气，正常喘。抓住我: Wayne Qiao fits the spare mask over the man's face and straps him to himself with two webbing straps: “Don't hold your breath, breathe normally. Grab my belt and don't let go, whatever you touch.”
strings.也许是地面停电了: Maybe the surface has lost power
strings.也许这是他留下的最后一样东西: Maybe this is the last thing he left behind
strings.二氧化碳已经浓到让人站不起来了：有人瘫在地上，怎么叫都叫不醒。: The carbon dioxide is now so thick that people can't stay on their feet: some lie slumped on the ground and can't be roused.
strings.井下 450 米。2 号上山坡度八度左右，是条死头巷道，尽头比运输大巷高出二十来: 450 metres underground. The No. 2 Rise climbs at about eight degrees and is a dead end; its far end is some twenty metres above the main haulage roadway. Where the rise meets the main roadway at the bottom is the lowest point of the whole drift, and it is now completely under water. In the coal wall at the far end is a brick seal, and behind it an abandoned crosscut leading to the old 1201 district next door.
strings.井下 450 米，水还在涨，空气一天比一天稠。地面的钻机，正在找你们。: Four hundred and fifty metres down, the water is still rising and the air grows thicker by the day. Up on the surface, a drill is looking for you.
strings.井下二十六七度，潮得能拧出水来。你们有三个饭盒、半袋饼干、两包方便面、几个水壶里: It is twenty-six or twenty-seven degrees down here, and damp enough to wring water out of the air. You have three lunch tins, half a bag of biscuits, two packs of instant noodles, what is left in a few water bottles, and seven cap lamps—most of a shift's charge already gone. The compressed-air line runs from your feet all the way to the shaft bottom, but not a breath comes out of it now. In the coal wall at the far end there is a brick seal closing off an old crosscut, abandoned years ago; a grey rat with a bald tail crouches on the highest roof beam, as trapped as you are. The people on the surface know something has happened, but they don't know whether you are alive, let alone where you are.
strings.井下恒温约 26°C、湿度饱和：不怕冷，但淋水会让人湿透。顶板淋水从岩层里渗下来: It is a steady 26°C underground and the air is saturated: cold is no danger, but the roof drips will soak you through. Roof water seeps down through the rock and is fairly clean; the old-workings water at your feet is acidic, full of iron and bacteria, and drinking much of it brings on diarrhoea and dehydration.
strings.井下没有。只能等地面送下来。: There are none underground. You can only wait for the surface to send some down.
strings.井下没有外包不外包，一样分: Underground, contract crew or not, everyone gets the same share
strings.井下的老鼠: A rat that lives in the mine
strings.人人都饿，谁也顾不上谁: Everyone's hungry; nobody can look after anybody
strings.人命一样金贵: Every life is worth the same
strings.人已经很虚了，拖过来也不一定救得活；墙里的气照样会涌出来: He's too far gone already; dragging him over might not save him—and the gas behind the wall will pour out anyway
strings.人都困在这儿了，出去再说: Everyone's trapped down here. Sort it out once we're out
strings.什么也不解释，今天就下水: No explanations. Go into the water today
strings.什么也别问，让他把手机收好: Don't ask anything; tell him to put the phone away
strings.什么也没有了，只能硬扛: There's nothing left. You just tough it out
strings.什么都不消耗，可伤腿一直错着位: Costs nothing, but the broken leg stays out of line
strings.今天全班一起动手修: The whole crew fixes it today
strings.从今天起，巷道里只留一盏灯，挂在最高的那根棚梁上。: From today, only one lamp stays lit in the roadway, hung on the highest roof beam.
strings.从支护用的坑木上剥下树皮，刮出里面一层发白的嫩皮，再用镐尖刮些木屑，泡软了嚼。嫩: Peel the bark off the pit props, scrape out the pale inner layer, and scrape off some sawdust with the tip of a pick to soak and chew. The inner bark has a little starch; the sawdust only fills you up. Strip too much and the supports weaken; eat too much and it can block your gut.
strings.他今年才十七岁。下井用的是表哥罗国庆的身份证——矿上不收不满十八的，是韦德贵托外: He is only seventeen. He came down on his cousin George Luo's ID card—the mine won't take anyone under eighteen, and Doug Wei got the contractor to arrange it. His mother has always believed he washes dishes in a restaurant in the county town.
strings.他们把矿长的信原样塞回钻杆，又附上了一张纸——田立新写的，透水前三天的隐患记录。: They push the mine manager's letter back up the drill rod as it is, and tie on another sheet—Leon Tian's, the hazard record from three days before the inrush.
strings.他冲进了水边的烂泥里，腿被水下的铁器划开了一道口子。: He plunges into the mud at the water's edge; something iron under the water opens a gash in his leg.
strings.他娘能找对人，矿上和外包队要为用童工担责；石磊怕矿被关，韦德贵帮他办假身份的事也: His mother can find the right people, and the mine and the contractor will answer for putting a minor underground; Larry Shi is afraid the mine will be shut, and the false ID Doug Wei got him will come out too
strings.他把位置和伤情带上去，指挥部会把水泵和人手往这条大巷调；他的气瓶，也只够一个来回: He carries the position and the injuries up top; the command will move pumps and men to this main roadway. And his tank holds one round trip, no more
strings.他是以“罗国庆”的名字被抬上井的。补偿款打到了表哥的卡上，表哥分了他一半。后来他: He was carried out of the shaft under the name George Luo. The compensation went into his cousin's bank account, and the cousin gave him half. He never went underground again; he tightens screws in an electronics factory in Dongguan. On night shift, he always turns the lamp at his workstation up as bright as it goes.
strings.他那份减半，省下来给正式工: Halve his share; keep it for the company men
strings.伤口被一遍遍冲洗，挤出了脓，重新包好。: The wound is rinsed again and again, the pus pressed out, and bound up fresh.
strings.伤员和最虚弱的先走: The injured and the weakest go first
strings.伤员被裹上保温毯，抬上了第一趟小艇。剩下的人一直望着那束灯光，直到它拐过弯去。一: The injured are wrapped in thermal blankets and lifted onto the first boat. The rest watch that light until it turns the bend. A little over an hour later, the engine sounds again.
strings.伤得最重的人戴上了自救器，胸口一起一伏，总算没断了那口气。: The most badly hurt man is put on a self-rescuer; his chest rises and falls—at least the breath hasn't stopped.
strings.你们七个人在迎头最里面，退路被水截断了，只能顺着 2 号上山往高处跑。上山是条死: The seven of you were at the very end of the heading. The water cut off the way out, so you ran up the No. 2 Rise to higher ground. The rise is a dead end; its far end is about twenty metres higher than the main roadway at the bottom of the slope, and the water chased you to within three or four metres of your feet before it slowed. Eddie Ho, the gas inspector, was knocked over by the water and thrown against the scraper conveyor; his leg is broken, and the others dragged him up. Manny, the boy from the contract crew, was hauled up the slope by Doug Wei with one hand, and his own hands are still shaking.
strings.你们被救了上来：{survivors}。没能上来的：{dead}。三个月后，事故: You were brought up alive: {survivors}. Those who weren't: {dead}. Three months on, the investigation report came out: the 1203 face had shown clear signs before the flood; the mine hid them and kept producing. The manager was held on criminal charges, and the torn-out hazard page became the key evidence. Nobody who told the truth got off lightly—yet every Qingming, someone stands a long time at those new graves behind the hill.
strings.你吃一点，他欠你一个人情，也捏着你一个把柄: You eat a little; he owes you a favour, and you've got a hold over him
strings.你的胶靴筒里藏着一个打火机和半包烟。下井严禁带烟火，可你抽了一辈子，每回都偷偷带: Down in your rubber boot you've hidden a lighter and half a pack of cigarettes. Smoking materials are strictly banned underground, but you've smoked all your life and always sneaked them down, slipping off to the return airway for a few drags. Now the roof of this roadway is full of methane.
strings.你自己少吃一口（约 150 千卡）: You go without a mouthful yourself (about 150 kcal)
strings.信被折好，塞进了一个人胸前的口袋。谁也没再提起它。: The letter is folded away and tucked into a pocket against someone's chest. Nobody brings it up again.
strings.借着灯给家里写回信: Write a reply home by lamplight
strings.先别动他，等救援来了再说: Don't touch him yet; wait for the rescue team
strings.先别回，出去再说: Don't write back yet. Sort it out once we're out
strings.先架棚撑住顶板，再刨人: Set props to hold the roof first, then dig him out
strings.先给伤员和最虚的人: The injured and the weakest first
strings.全挤到巷道最尽头的高处: Crowd onto the high ground at the very end of the roadway
strings.全班唯一的瓦检员，揣着一台瓦斯便携仪——大家看到的氧气、二氧化碳、瓦斯读数全靠它: The crew's only gas inspector, and he carries the handheld methane detector—every oxygen, carbon dioxide and methane reading the group sees comes from it. When the water came he was knocked over and thrown against the scraper conveyor: an open fracture of the right shin, the bone through the skin. His chest took a blow too; he can't get his breath, and there is blood in what he coughs up. He is Felix Wang's apprentice.
strings.公共的吃的只剩下最后一个饭盒了，米饭已经发酸。所有人的眼睛都盯着它。: Only one lunch tin is left of the shared food, and the rice has turned sour. Every eye is on it.
strings.公平，可每人只分到一口: Fair, but everyone gets one mouthful
strings.公平，大家心里踏实；可谁身上还藏着什么，现在没人知道: Fair, and everyone can rest easy—but nobody knows yet what else anyone is hiding
strings.再留两天，等最难熬的时候: Keep it two more days, for the worst of it
strings.再等等，等地面来人: Wait a little longer, for the surface to come
strings.再等等：等绳子搓好、水再退一点: Wait: for the rope to be finished, and the water to drop a little more
strings.写张纸条送上去：下面还有一个韦德贵: Send a note up: there's still a Doug Wei down here
strings.冷的、生的，也比炸死强: Cold and raw is better than blown to bits
strings.冷静、话少、动作利索；什么事都先看、先量、再说；对规程比田立新还较真，可他见过太: Calm, terse, quick-handed; looks, measures, then speaks. A bigger stickler for the regulations than Leon Tian—but he has seen too many men carried out to believe the regulations can save everyone.
strings.几个人把他按住，抱紧: Hold him down, hold him tight
strings.几个人把他按回了木板上。赵存柱没再争，只是一整夜都睁着眼睛，盯着坡下的水。: They press him back down onto the plank. Charlie Zhao doesn't argue again; he just lies with his eyes open all night, watching the water below the slope.
strings.几个人轮流抡着镐，顺着那道缝往里刨。: They take turns swinging the pick, digging in along the crack.
strings.几个大男人抱在一起，哭得像孩子。: Grown men hold each other and cry like children.
strings.出去以后也许用得上: Might be useful once we're out
strings.分吃的的时候，有人嘀咕了一句：“外包队的，凭啥跟咱们分一样多？他又不是矿上的人。: When the food is shared out, someone mutters: “Contract crew—why should he get the same share as us? He isn't one of the mine's own.” Doug Wei pinches his one small piece of biscuit and says nothing.
strings.刚结婚两个月，媳妇怀孕三个月。下井才一年多，为的是攒钱在县城买套房。全班力气最大: Married two months ago; his wife is three months pregnant. He's been underground just over a year, saving for a flat in the county town. The strongest man in the crew—he can shoulder two pit props at once.
strings.别动，我先看看。……收到，上面听得见。: Don't move, let me look first. …Copy, they can hear us up top.
strings.别瞎想，省着力气等: Don't think about it. Save your strength and wait
strings.别费劲了，地面的压风机八成早停了: Don't bother—the compressor up top is probably off by now
strings.别高兴得太早，省着力气: Don't celebrate too soon. Save your strength
strings.化学氧自救器，戴上能呼吸四十五分钟左右的氧气。贺小勇那台被水冲丢了。: Chemical-oxygen self-rescuers, each good for about forty-five minutes of oxygen. Eddie Ho's was washed away.
strings.十年前在贵州一个小煤窑，你也遇过透水。那一次你是自己憋着气，从淹了的巷道底下潜了: Ten years ago, at a small pit in Guizhou, you went through a flood like this one. That time you held your breath and swam more than thirty metres through a flooded roadway to get out—the only one who survived. Your cousin had hurt his leg and couldn't swim; you didn't look back. You've never told anyone.
strings.十年里，韦德贵第二次一个人从淹了的井下活着出来。他抱着小满的骨灰回了毕节，跪在小: For the second time in ten years, Doug Wei came out of a flooded mine alive and alone. He carried Manny's ashes back to Bijie and knelt at the door of the boy's mother, unable to say a word. After that he never travelled far again. He builds walls for people in his township and won't go down into a cellar.
strings.半个多月后，水终于退了。救护队员在 2 号上山的尽头找到了他们：几个人挨在一起，: More than half a month later, the water finally went down. The rescue team found them at the end of the No. 2 Rise: several men huddled together, one man's hand still resting on the compressed-air line, a pick handle thrown down at their feet. On the roof beam beside them, someone had written the names of his family in chalk, stroke by stroke.
strings.半夜，{actor} 听见石磊那边“咔哒”一声——像是铝饭盒盖子扣上的声音。郝建: In the middle of the night, {actor} hears a click from Larry Shi's side of the roadway—like an aluminium lunch tin lid snapping shut. James Hao's tin is nowhere to be found; anyone who has been underground knows that sound.
strings.半夜，小满饿得蜷成一团，咬着袖口不出声，肚子却叫得整条巷子都听得见。他是这里头最: In the middle of the night, Manny curls up tight with hunger, biting his sleeve to keep quiet, but his stomach growls loud enough for the whole roadway to hear. He is the youngest of them and eats the most—he is still growing.
strings.半夜，巷道尽头那道砖砌的密闭墙后面传来了敲击声——三长两短，跟你们敲管子的节奏一: In the middle of the night, knocking comes from behind the brick seal at the end of the roadway—three long, two short, exactly the rhythm you knock on the pipe. Then a hoarse voice: “Anyone there… I'm from the 1201 haulage crew…” Behind the wall is a crosscut abandoned years ago. The regulations are clear: what is pent up behind a seal is methane and dead air, and without testing, nobody touches it.
strings.半夜，有人听见韦德贵那边窸窸窣窣地嚼东西。第二天，没人愿意挨着他坐。: In the middle of the night, someone hears Doug Wei chewing something, soft and furtive. The next day, nobody wants to sit next to him.
strings.半夜，有人把耳朵贴在煤壁上，猛地坐了起来：“听！”——很远很远的地方，传来有节奏: In the middle of the night, someone presses an ear to the coal wall and sits bolt upright: “Listen!”—far, far away comes a steady rhythm of vibration, thump… thump… thump… It's the drill. The surface is drilling down.
strings.半夜，灰子突然在棚梁上乱窜，吱吱尖叫，一头钻进了尽头煤帮的一道裂缝，再也没出来。: In the middle of the night, Smoky suddenly races along the roof beams, squealing, then bolts into a crack in the coal wall at the far end and does not come out again. In the dark, someone props himself up: “The rat's gone… The old-timers say when the rat goes, this place won't hold much longer.”
strings.压风管的阀门被冲下来的矸石砸扁了，管口也堵满了煤泥。拆下阀门、掏净淤堵、接好管头: Rock that came down with the water has flattened the valve on the compressed-air line, and the open end is packed with coal slurry. Take the valve off, clear the blockage, fit a new end—and if the compressor on the surface is running and the section under the water isn't broken, fresh air will come through.
strings.压风管里的“嘶嘶”声突然停了。巷道里一下子静得吓人，所有人都屏住了呼吸，等着它再: The hiss in the compressed-air line stops dead. The roadway goes frighteningly quiet; everyone holds their breath, waiting for it to start again.
strings.原型：2010 年 3 月 28 日山西王家岭煤矿透水事故，153 人被困，11: Inspired by: the Wangjialing mine flood in Shanxi on 28 March 2010. 153 men were trapped and 115 were brought out alive after eight days underground. Some strapped themselves to the roof supports with their belts so they could sleep without sliding into the water; they ate sawdust, bark and paper when they were hungry, drank mine water when they were thirsty, and took turns switching on their cap lamps. In 2010, 33 miners were trapped 700 metres down by a collapse at the San José copper mine in Chile; it was 17 days before a borehole reached them, and until then each man ate two small spoonfuls of tuna every 48 hours. Their shift boss, Luis Urzúa, kept strict discipline over the rations, and all 33 came out after 69 days. In 2021, an explosion at the Hushan gold mine in Qixia, Shandong trapped 22 workers; rescuers drilled a borehole “lifeline” and sent down food, medicine and letters from home, and 11 were eventually saved.
strings.又过了一天，小洞那头再也没有人来接水壶了。{actor} 把耳朵贴在砖墙上听了很: Another day passes, and no one on the far side of the hole comes for the water bottle again. {actor} presses an ear to the brick wall and listens for a long time, then scoops up a handful of coal slurry and plasters the hole shut.
strings.叔，等出去了，我请你们吃毕节烙锅——洋芋、豆腐、肥肠，一锅烙得滋滋响。: Uncle, when we get out I'll treat you all to Bijie griddle pot—potatoes, tofu, pork intestines, all sizzling on the iron.
strings.只写“我们都还活着”，别的出去再说: Write only “We're all still alive”—the rest can wait until we're out
strings.只开一盏，轮流开，睡觉时全关: One lamp only, taking turns, all off while you sleep
strings.只掏一个小洞，先递水过去，墙别拆: Make a small hole only, pass water through first—don't break the seal
strings.只能等地面送药下来: Wait for the surface to send medicine down
strings.只要不出一点火星: As long as there's not a spark
strings.可不敢睡死了，睡死了就醒不过来了。: Don't you dare sleep too deep. Sleep too deep and you won't wake up.
strings.各人有各人的难处: Every man has his own troubles
strings.各人的饭盒各人留着: Everyone keeps their own lunch tin
strings.名字是这孩子的饭碗：出去以后他还能接着打工，补偿也照名单发；可这笔账，早晚得有人: The name is the boy's living: out there he can keep working, and the compensation is paid out by the list—but that account will have to be settled one day
strings.含一块煤，慢慢嚼: Hold a lump of coal in your mouth, chew it slowly
strings.听王福山的：钻机还会回来的: Listen to Felix Wang: the drill will come back
strings.听见了不等于找到了: Hearing it isn't the same as being found
strings.和身边的人说说话: Talk to the man beside you
strings.咱敲，使劲敲。上头的人耳朵灵着呢。: Knock. Knock hard. The ones up top have sharp ears.
strings.咳嗽声在黑暗里响了一整夜，没人说话。: The coughing goes on all night in the dark. Nobody speaks.
strings.嚼烟盒、本子上的纸: Chew the cigarette packet, paper from the notebook
strings.回信上只写了一个字：“行。”: The reply that goes up carries one word: “Fine.”
strings.回条上写着：“下面这个叫罗小满，贵州毕节人，十七岁。他娘的信收到了，人还活着。”: The note that comes back reads: “The one down there is Manny Luo, from Bijie in Guizhou, seventeen years old. His mother's letter has been received, and he is alive.” Manny stares at the line and cries like a child—he is a child.
strings.回条上写着：“罗国庆，活着。”小满把那封信叠成小小的一块，塞进了贴身的口袋。: The note that comes back reads: “George Luo, alive.” Manny folds the letter into a small square and tucks it into the pocket inside his jacket.
strings.在井下干了二十三年，从推车工干到班长，全队出了名的能吃苦、能拿主意。说话算数，班: Twenty-three years underground, from tub pusher to crew boss; known across the section for hard work and quick decisions. His word holds, and the crew follows him. He was the last one out when the water came, and his left hand was laid open on the wire mesh.
strings.在平台下方用煤块、矸石和装满煤的编织袋垒一道墙，抹上煤泥堵缝。挡不住大水，但水慢: Build a wall below the platform out of coal, rock and woven sacks filled with coal, and pack the gaps with slurry. It won't hold back a flood, but while the water creeps up it can buy you another metre or so.
strings.在平台下方用煤块、矸石和装满煤的编织袋垒墙，抹上煤泥堵缝。挡不住大水，可水慢慢涨: Build a wall below the platform out of coal, rock and woven sacks filled with coal, and pack the gaps with slurry. It won't hold back a flood, but while the water creeps up it can buy you another metre or so.
strings.在水边摸了半天，只摸到一手煤泥: Groped along the water's edge for ages and came up with nothing but a handful of coal slurry
strings.在煤帮上划一道粉笔印，盯着水位: Chalk a line on the coal wall and watch the water level
strings.在这座山底下挖了三十六年煤，矿上的老巷道、老空区都装在他脑子里。一期尘肺，爬几步: Thirty-six years digging coal under this mountain; every old roadway and old working in the mine is mapped in his head. Stage-one black lung: a few steps uphill and he's gasping, and once he starts coughing he can't stop. Two years from retirement. Eddie Ho is the apprentice he trained.
strings.地面也许会加泵: The surface might send more pumps
strings.地面会重新定位，再打一个孔: The surface can fix the position and drill another hole
strings.地面往下打的钻孔。你们只能凭声音判断它打到了哪儿——也不知道它是不是冲着你们来的: The borehole being drilled down from the surface. You can only guess from the sound how far it has got—or whether it's even aimed at you.
strings.地面救援指挥部对你们位置的把握。规律的敲击声是最主要的线索。: How sure the rescue command on the surface is of where you are. Steady knocking is the main clue.
strings.地面钻孔每天往下打 60–100 米，要打 450 米。能不能打中你们，取决于救: The surface borehole goes down 60–100 metres a day and has 450 metres to cover. Whether it hits you depends on how well the rescue command has fixed your position—and steady knocking is the main clue. Once the borehole breaks through, it becomes a “lifeline” for air, food, medicine and letters from home.
strings.坡下传来一阵闷响，像是又有一片老空区被泡塌了。水声一下子大了，水面眼看着往上爬。: A dull boom comes from down the slope, as if another stretch of old workings has caved in under the water. The sound of the water swells, and the surface climbs before your eyes.
strings.坡下传来哗哗的水声，水势又大了，水面在一点点往上爬。: Water roars at the bottom of the slope. The flow is up again and the surface is creeping higher.
strings.坡底的水面上冒起一串气泡，一束光从水底亮了起来——一个戴着全面罩、背着气瓶的人浮: A string of bubbles breaks the surface at the bottom of the slope, and a light comes up from under the water—a man in a full-face mask, a tank on his back, surfaces with a guide rope tied round his waist. He spits out the mouthpiece and takes two breaths: “Provincial rescue corps—Wayne Qiao. Charlie Zhao sent me. He crawled out through the main roadway and he's alive; they're searching for Benny and the rest too.” He says his spare mask can take one man out under the water: forty-odd metres, and at the narrowest point you have to go through sideways.
