He spits out the mouthpiece and takes two breaths: “Provincial rescue corps—Wayne Qiao. The borehole has been positioned; the rescue command sent me in first to take a look.” He says his spare mask can take one man out under the water: forty-odd metres, and at the narrowest point you have to go through sideways.
strings.墙那边的敲击声一天比一天稀。从小洞里递过去的水，赵存柱只喝了一半：“我……我自己: The knocking on the far side of the wall grows fainter by the day. Of the water passed through the small hole, Charlie Zhao drinks only half: “I… I can't crawl any more. If you get out, tell my mother—Charlie and Benny…” He doesn't finish; only the coughing is left.
strings.复位，用掉急救包: Set the bone and use up the first-aid kit
strings.多一个懂行的人：伤员有人照看，顶板有人盯着；也多一个人分空气: One more man who knows the mine: someone to tend the injured, someone to watch the roof—and one more man taking air
strings.多喝水，硬扛: Drink plenty of water and tough it out
strings.夜里，灰子顺着棚梁来回乱窜，吱吱地叫个不停，怎么赶也不走。有人盯着顶板看了很久：: In the night Smoky races back and forth along the roof beams, squeaking and squeaking, and won't be shooed away. Someone stares up at the roof for a long time: “When the rats move house, the roof's coming down.”
strings.夜里，韦德贵摸了摸贴身口袋里那几个早就压扁了的馒头——外包队的人吃不上食堂，每天: In the night Doug Wei feels the few steamed buns in the pocket against his chest, long since flattened—the contract crew get no canteen, so they bring their own food in every day. The day the food was counted, he didn't put them out. So far, nobody knows.
strings.大家会知道你有本事，也会知道你丢下过人: Everyone will know what you can do—and that you left a man behind
strings.大家会记住这件事（每个馒头约 220 千卡）: Everyone will remember this (each steamed bun is about 220 kcal)
strings.大家往下挪了十几米，离水边更近了。头不那么胀了，胸口却更闷。: They move a dozen metres down the slope, closer to the water. Their heads throb less, but their chests feel tighter.
strings.大家把仅有的一点东西搬到巷道尽头，然后坐着，看水一点点漫上来。: They carry what little they have to the end of the roadway, then sit and watch the water creep up.
strings.大家把几截粉笔头攥在手心里抓阄。抓到最后一趟的人笑了笑，说：“都等了这么多天了。: They draw lots with the chalk stubs closed in their fists. The man who draws the last trip smiles and says: “We've waited all these days already.”
strings.大家把坑木、木板和装满煤的编织袋往上扛，在巷道尽头垫出了一块高出半米的平台。: They haul pit props, planks and woven sacks of coal up the slope and build a platform half a metre higher at the end of the roadway.
strings.大家把巷道尽头那道透着点凉气的裂缝口让给了他。: They give him the crack at the end of the roadway where a little cool air comes through.
strings.大家约好，每到整点敲一轮“三长两短”。: They agree to knock a round of “three long, two short” every hour on the hour.
strings.大家轮流用湿毛巾给他擦身子降温。: They take turns sponging him down with wet towels to bring the fever down.
strings.大家退到了几米外。等顶板不再掉渣，再回去刨的时候，煤堆下面已经没了动静。: They fall back a few metres. When the roof stops shedding and they go back to dig, there's no sound left under the coal.
strings.大家都会累得够呛，还要费不少灯（矿灯电量 −3）；修好了也不一定有风: Everyone will be worn out, and it will use up a lot of lamp charge (lamp charge −3); even repaired, there may be no air
strings.大家都睡了。王福山摸着胶靴筒里的打火机和那半包烟，烟瘾犯得手直抖——抽一口，也许: Everyone is asleep. Felix Wang feels the lighter and the half pack of cigarettes in his rubber boot; the craving sets his hand shaking—one drag, and maybe he lasts the night. But he knows better than anyone what has gathered along the roof of this roadway.
strings.大家都难受，顾不上了: Everyone is suffering—no one can spare anything
strings.大巷那段我熟：四百米，两个弯，最低的地方在 3 号联络巷口。: I know that stretch of the main roadway: four hundred metres, two bends, and the lowest point's at the mouth of No. 3 crosscut.
strings.天亮之前，赵存柱悄悄下了水。: Before daylight, Charlie Zhao slips into the water.
strings.天亮的时候，赵存柱躺过的那块木板空了。坡下的水边扔着他的胶靴，靴子里塞着一张烟盒: At dawn the plank where Charlie Zhao lay is empty. His rubber boots lie at the water's edge, a cigarette-packet paper stuffed in one, scrawled on with a lump of coal: “Benny, wait for me.”
strings.头顶的钻机声停了，一停就是一整天。没人知道上面出了什么事——钻头卡住了？孔塌了？: The drill overhead stops, and stays stopped all day. Nobody knows what has happened up there—the bit jammed? The hole collapsed? Or… have they stopped drilling?
strings.头顶的钻机声越来越响、越来越近……然后，在离你们二三十米远的地方停住了。过了很久: The drill overhead grows louder and nearer… then stops twenty or thirty metres away. After a long while, the drill rod starts to come back up. The borehole has missed—it has come down into the neighbouring roadway.
strings.学老辈人：用皮带把自己绑在顶板的棚梁上: Do it the old-timers' way: strap yourself to a roof beam with your belt
strings.守住规程，守住这口气；墙那边的人，就只能听天由命了: Keep to the regulations, keep this air; the man behind the wall can only leave it to fate
strings.安监站的安全员，那天正好下来查掘进面，结果和大家一起被堵在了里面。受过急救培训，: A safety inspector from the mine safety station who happened to come down that day to check the heading, and got trapped with everyone else. He has first-aid training and knows compressed air, drainage and every kind of instrument. Turned his right ankle in the retreat. He's written the crews plenty of fines, and he isn't well liked.
strings.小满把铅笔头含在嘴里想了很久，一笔一画地写，写完谁也没给看，就绑上了钻杆。: Manny holds the pencil stub in his mouth and thinks for a long time, then writes, stroke by stroke. When he has finished he shows nobody; he ties it to the drill rod.
strings.小满的脸一下子白了，半天才说：“十七……身份证是我表哥的。叔，你们莫说出去，说出: Manny's face goes white. It is a long moment before he speaks: “Seventeen… The ID card is my cousin's. Uncle, don't tell anyone. If this gets out, I'll have nothing to eat.”
strings.小满的遗物只有半包方便面调料、一部没电的旧手机，和那根一米一个疙瘩的导向绳。他娘: All Manny left was half a sachet of noodle seasoning, a dead old phone and the guide rope with a knot every metre. His mother came up from Bijie and sat outside the funeral home all night. Only later did she learn that on the day her son went underground, he had turned seventeen just a month before.
strings.就当是给他壮个胆: If only to keep his nerve up
strings.就打一次火，烤点热乎的: Strike one spark, cook something hot
strings.就按名单回：罗国庆，活着: Answer by the list: George Luo, alive
strings.屏幕亮起来的那一瞬间，一道蓝白色的火光贴着顶板横扫过去，紧接着是一声把人五脏六腑: The instant the screen lights up, a blue-white sheet of flame sweeps along the roof, and a boom follows that knocks a man's guts out of place—the methane has gone up.
strings.山西某县福源煤业 1203 工作面 2 号上山: No. 2 Rise, 1203 heading, Fuyuan Coal, a county in Shanxi
strings.巷道里只剩下滴水声和人的喘气声。: Nothing in the roadway but dripping water and breathing.
strings.巷道里只剩下粗重的喘气声。: All that is left in the roadway is heavy breathing.
strings.师傅，我腿……不疼了。真的。: Master, my leg… doesn't hurt now. Really.
strings.师徒俩是一块儿被抬上井的。王福山提前退了休，尘肺后来转成了二期，每天早上在院子里: Master and apprentice were carried up together. Felix Wang retired early; his black lung went to stage two. Every morning he coughs for a while in the yard, and then he phones Eddie Ho: “Going down today? What's the gas reading?”
strings.带他去刮树皮，教他怎么嚼木屑: Take him to scrape bark, teach him how to chew sawdust
strings.带河北口音的普通话，说话像下命令：“收到”“明白”“别动，我先看看”。: Mandarin with a Hebei accent; talks like he's giving orders: “Copy,” “Understood,” “Don't move, let me look first.”
strings.带着全班的人活着出去，而且不让人知道是你下令接着打的那一茬炮: Get the whole crew out alive—and never let anyone know you ordered that last round of shots
strings.干净的水喝光了，{actor} 渴得实在受不了，捧起坡下的积水喝了好几大口。半夜: The clean water is gone. {actor} can't stand the thirst any longer and gulps down several mouthfuls of the water at the bottom of the slope. In the middle of the night, the cramps start.
strings.平时全黑，只有干活时才开灯: Dark the rest of the time; lamps only for work
strings.年轻后生的口气，爱说“没问题”“包在我身上”，着急时骂一串。: Talks like the young lad he is: “No problem,” “Leave it to me.” Swears in long strings when he's anxious.
strings.开两盏，人心不能先黑了: Two lamps lit—let no heart go dark first
strings.开饭的时候，那只秃尾巴的灰老鼠又来了，蹲在离饭盒一臂远的地方，两只小眼睛盯着木板: When the food is shared out, the grey rat with the bald tail is back, crouched an arm's length from the lunch tin, its little eyes fixed on the biscuit crumbs on the plank. Someone says: “Old rule—you don't kill rats underground. While it's here, there's still air to breathe.” Someone else swallows: “It's still a good two mouthfuls of meat.”
strings.强势、护短、要面子；习惯拍板，不喜欢别人质疑他；心里压着事的时候话会变得特别多，: Forceful, protective of his own, proud; used to making the call and doesn't like being questioned. When something is weighing on him he talks more than usual and grabs the hardest jobs.
strings.当众问他撕掉的那页写了什么: Ask him in front of everyone what was on the torn-out page
strings.心里有数，可也更难熬: You'll know where you stand—which only makes it harder to bear
strings.悄悄扔进水里: Slip them into the water quietly
strings.悄悄收起来，留个把柄: Pocket it quietly—something to hold over him
strings.想想家里的人: Think about the people at home
strings.慢条斯理的晋北老汉腔，爱讲“老辈人说……”“井下的事，急不得”。: The slow drawl of an old northern Shanxi man. Fond of “The old-timers used to say…” and “Underground, you can't rush things.”
strings.憋一口气，顺着探明的水路从淹没段底下潜过去，到坡底另一头的大巷找救援队。最低的地: Take a breath and swim under the flooded stretch along the scouted route, to the main roadway on the far side of the slope, and find the rescuers. At the lowest point you'll be groping through twenty or thirty metres of black water, blind, the pressure stabbing at your ears. If you make it, everyone is saved; if you don't, you may never come back. The guide rope and a lower water level both improve the odds.
strings.憨直、话多、认死理；心里装着弟弟，一闲下来就念叨；一旦认准了一件事，九头牛也拉不: Simple, talkative, stubborn as a mule; his brother is always on his mind, and he goes on about him whenever there's a quiet moment. Once he has made up his mind, nine oxen couldn't pull him back.
strings.成了，两拨人都有救；不成，他就回不来了。探明的水路和导向绳能帮他一把（矿灯电量: If it works, both groups are saved; if not, he never comes back. The scouted route and the guide rope can help him (lamp charge −3, self-rescuer −1)
strings.成了，所有人有救；不成，就回不来了: If it works, everyone is saved; if not, he never comes back
strings.我不饿，真不饿……你们吃，我年轻，扛得住。: I'm not hungry, honest… you eat. I'm young, I can take it.
strings.我们班七个人，水一来就冲散了。存旺……存旺他们往老回风巷那头跑了，那头高。: Seven of us in the crew, and the water scattered us. Benny… Benny and the others ran for the old return airway. It's higher over there.
strings.我在部队潜过三十米深的海，没潜过这么黑的水。: I've dived thirty metres in the sea in the navy. Never in water this black.
strings.我娘以为我在县城饭馆里洗碗。要是她晓得了……: My mum thinks I'm washing dishes in a restaurant in town. If she finds out…
strings.我娘就俩儿子。我得把存旺带回去，不然我没脸进家门。: My mum's only got two sons. I've got to bring Benny home, or I can't show my face at the door.
strings.我数到一千了，钻机还没响。我再数一千。: I've counted to a thousand and the drill still hasn't started. I'll count another thousand.
strings.所有人一直干到半夜，墙垒起了半人高，手指头都磨出了血。: They work on until the middle of the night; the dam stands half a man high and their fingers are rubbed bloody.
strings.所有人一起干，墙能多垒一截: With everyone at it, the dam goes up another good stretch
strings.所有人一起拼命敲，让他们听出偏在哪: Everyone knock for all they're worth—let them hear where it went wide
strings.所有人围着那截管子干了大半天：拆阀门、掏煤泥、找能用的管头。: They spend most of a day working round that length of pipe: taking the valve off, digging out the coal slurry, finding an end that will do.
strings.所有人干到半夜，挡水墙一下子能垒起一大截: With everyone at it till midnight, the dam goes up a whole stretch at once
strings.所有人挤在巷道尽头不到十平米的地方，腿压着腿，谁也睡不着。: They crowd into a space less than ten square metres at the end of the roadway, legs on top of legs, and nobody can sleep.
strings.所有人蜷在地上，一动不动地等着那股甜味散去。: Everyone curls up on the ground and lies still, waiting for the sweet smell to fade.
strings.所有人跪在煤堆上用手刨。被压住的人被一点点拖了出来，脸上全是血和煤。: Everyone kneels on the coal pile and digs with their hands. The buried man is dragged out little by little, his face all blood and coal.
strings.所有人躺下，少喘气，等: Everyone lie down, breathe less, wait
strings.所有人躺下，少说话、少动: Everyone lie down, talk less, move less
strings.所有人躺下，少说话、少喘气: Everyone lie down, talk less, breathe less
strings.所有人轮流敲管子，一刻也不停: Everyone take turns knocking the pipe, never stopping
strings.所有人都喝撑了。到了半夜，有人开始心慌、手脚抽筋，喘不上气。: Everyone drinks until they are bloated. By the middle of the night, some are panicking, their hands and feet cramping, gasping for breath.
strings.所有人都头疼得像要裂开，喘气越来越急，干一点活心就跳得厉害，嘴唇发乌。便携仪上的: Everyone's head feels ready to split, their breathing comes faster and faster, the least work sets their hearts hammering, and their lips are turning blue. The carbon dioxide on the handheld detector has reached {var.co2}. Leon Tian says: “There isn't enough air.”
strings.所有人都扑到了墙上，一袋一袋地往上垒煤。: Everyone throws themselves at the wall, stacking sacks of coal one after another.
strings.所有人都躺了下来，听着自己的心跳。: Everyone lies down and listens to their own heartbeat.
strings.所有吃的喝的都交出来，统一分: Hand over all the food and water and share it out
strings.所有矿灯剩下的电，按一盏灯亮一小时算。灯全灭了，就是伸手不见五指。: The charge left in all the cap lamps, counted as hours of one lamp burning. When they're all out, you won't see your hand in front of your face.
strings.手机屏幕的光冷冷的，照着一张张脸。小满把亮度调到最低攥在手心里，谁要去哪儿，他就: The phone screen glows cold on face after face. Manny turns the brightness down to its lowest and keeps it cupped in his hand; whenever anyone needs to go somewhere, he lights the way.
strings.手机里放的是一首山歌，声音开到最小。照片一张张翻过去：贵州的山，一栋没刷墙的砖房: A mountain song plays from the phone, turned down as low as it will go. The photos go past one by one: the hills of Guizhou, a brick house with unplastered walls, a woman with a cloth wrapped round her head. Manny says: “That's my mum.”
strings.打开一盏灯，让他看见大家: Light one lamp so he can see the others
strings.打火机的火比电池稳；可瓦斯不认这个: A lighter flame is steadier than a battery—but methane doesn't care
strings.打着灯顺着水边找他: Take a lamp and search the waterline for him
strings.打着矿灯顺坡摸到水边，用铁丝钩子捞漂过来的东西：饭盒、水壶、矿灯、工具……也可能: Take a lamp down the slope to the water's edge and fish for whatever has floated in with a wire hook: lunch tins, water bottles, lamps, tools… or something that chills you to the bone. The air is worst at the water's edge, and your feet sink in mud.
strings.把东西都搬到最高处，听天由命: Move everything to the highest ground and trust to luck
strings.把他的胶靴收好，出去了交给他家里: Keep his rubber boots safe; give them to his family if we get out
strings.把信和真相一起送上去: Send the letter and the truth up together
strings.把剩下的自救器给伤得最重的人: Give the remaining self-rescuers to the worst injured
strings.把家信读了一遍又一遍: Read the letter from home over and over
strings.把想说的话都写下来: Write down everything you want to say
strings.把打火机和烟交出来，说清楚: Hand over the lighter and the cigarettes, and come clean
strings.把握大一点再下水: Go in when the odds are better
strings.把握大一点再下水；就怕他等不起，大家也等不起: Go in when the odds are better; but he can't wait that long, and neither can the others
strings.把矿上早就知道有透水征兆的事写上去: Write in that the mine knew about the warning signs all along
strings.把自己明天那口吃的分给他: Give him your own ration for tomorrow
strings.把自救器给最难受的人戴上: Put the self-rescuer on the worst-off man
strings.把被水泡软、被压裂的坑木换下来，用剩下的木料和钢梁重新架棚、打木楔。顶板来压的时: Replace the waterlogged and cracked pit props, re-set the arches with the timber and steel that's left, and drive in wedges. When the roof is weighting, the supports are your life.
strings.把风筒布撕成条，和废电缆拧在一起，搓一根四五十米长的绳子。潜水的人拴着它，在黑水: Tear duct cloth into strips and twist them together with scrap cable into a rope forty or fifty metres long. Tied round a diver's waist, it's the only way to keep your bearings in the black water; if something goes wrong, the people above can haul him back. It can be done in the dark.
strings.把风筒布撕成条，和捞上来的废电缆拧在一起，搓一根四五十米长的绳子。潜水的人腰上拴: Tear duct cloth into strips and twist them together with the scrap cable you've fished out, into a rope forty or fifty metres long. Tied round a diver's waist, it's the only way to keep your bearings in the black water—and if something goes wrong, the people above can haul him back.
strings.把饭盒、水壶和安全帽挪到淋水最大的几处锚杆下面接水，接满了再倒进水壶。顶板淋水是: Move the lunch tins, water bottles and hard hats under the roof bolts that drip the most, and pour the water into the bottles as they fill. Roof water seeps down through the rock and is much cleaner than the water at your feet. When the roof is dripping hard you catch a lot; when it's still, only the odd drop.
strings.报平安：几个人、伤情、缺什么: Report you're alive: how many, injuries, what you need
strings.抱在一起哭了一场: They held each other and wept
strings.拆开密闭，把人拖过来: Break open the brick seal and drag him over
strings.拦住他：这只手、这副肺，潜不过去: Hold him back: that hand and those lungs will never make the dive
strings.拼命敲管子——告诉上面，下面快没气了: Bang the pipe for all you're worth—tell them up top we're running out of air
strings.拼命敲管子，告诉地面又来水了: Bang the pipe for all you're worth—tell the surface the water's coming in again
strings.拿出来，分给大家: Bring it out and share it out
strings.挡水墙垒到了齐胸高。墙那边的水拍着煤袋子，墙这边，总算有了一块干地方。: The dam is chest-high now. On the far side the water slaps against the coal sacks; on this side there's finally a patch of dry ground.
strings.接下来几天每个人的耗氧少两成，可活就干不了多少了: For the next few days every man burns a fifth less oxygen—but little work gets done
strings.撤退的时候，你顺手把班长搁在刮板机机头上的饭盒揣进了怀里（大约 650 千卡）。: During the retreat you scooped up the crew boss's lunch tin from the head of the scraper conveyor and tucked it inside your jacket (about 650 kcal). When everyone counted up the food later, you said nothing.
strings.放了它——老辈人说，有老鼠的地方就有活路: Let it go—the old-timers say where there's a rat there's a way to live
strings.教人自己找吃的；你也得陪着熬半宿: Teach them to find their own food; you'll be up half the night with them
strings.敲出人数，让他们知道下面有几个人: Knock out the head count so they know how many are down here
strings.敲击声一直响到所有人都抬不起胳膊。很久以后，地面上的钻机又转了起来——这一次，声: The knocking went on until no one could lift an arm. A long time after, the drill on the surface started up again—and this time the sound seemed a little closer.
strings.敲击声又急又乱。很久以后，坡下的水声好像小了一点。: The knocking turned frantic and ragged. A long time after, the water below the slope seemed a little quieter.
strings.敲击声在巷道里回荡。到了后半夜，头顶的震动又一下一下地响了起来。: The knocking echoed down the roadway. In the small hours the tremor overhead started up again, thud after thud.
strings.敲完一轮，所有人都屏住了呼吸。几秒钟后，管子里传来了回应：“咚、咚、咚。”——地: When the round was done, every man held his breath. Seconds later an answer came down the pipe: “Thud. Thud. Thud.”—someone up top had heard them!
strings.敲管子——盼着他过去了: Knock the pipe—praying he got through
strings.敲管子，催地面赶紧把压风机开起来: Knock the pipe—urge the surface to get the compressor running
strings.敲管子，告诉地面水没退: Knock the pipe—tell the surface the water hasn't dropped
strings.早一点被找到，才是真的有救: Being found sooner is the only real rescue
strings.晋北口音，嗓门大，爱说“咱”“甚”“可不敢”，话没说完先咳上一阵。: A loud northern Shanxi voice; says “us lot”, “what’s that” and “don't you dare”; usually coughs halfway through a sentence.
strings.晋北口音，说话短促有力，爱说“听我的”“没事，有我”，急了骂一句“球”。: A northern Shanxi accent; short, hard sentences. Likes “Do as I say” and “It's fine, I've got it.” Swears when he's rattled.
strings.普通话夹着晋中口音，爱引用“规程上写着……”，开口前常先叹一口气。: Mandarin with a central Shanxi accent; fond of quoting “The regulations say…”; often sighs before he speaks.
strings.最后一批人撤出 2 号上山的时候，有人回头看了一眼：那块摆过饭盒的木板空了。后来: When the last of them left the No. 2 Rise, someone looked back: the plank where the lunch tins had stood was empty. Later, when the mine cleared the roadway, several men said they'd seen a grey rat with a bald tail there. Nobody touched it. You don't kill rats underground—that's the old rule.
strings.最好的处理；可以后再有人受伤，就没有急救用品了: The best care possible; but if anyone else is hurt later, there's no first aid left
strings.最能干的人吃饱了，大家才有指望: Only if the ablest man eats does anyone stand a chance
strings.最虚弱的那个人被扶起来，先喝了第一口。: The weakest of them was propped up and drank the first mouthful.
strings.最虚的人多喝一些，其他人少一点: The weakest drink more, the others a little less
strings.最要紧的是让地面知道该怎么救: What matters most is letting the surface know how to get you out
strings.最需要救治的人先走: The ones who need treatment most go first
strings.有人在黑暗里闻到了烟味。: Someone smelled smoke in the dark.
strings.有人把便携仪塞进了衣服里，报警声闷闷地响了一夜。: Someone stuffed the detector inside his jacket, and the alarm whined, muffled, all night.
strings.有人把话顶了回去：“到了这底下，谁不是一条命？”韦德贵抬头看了说话的人一眼。: Someone shot back: “Down here, who's got more than one life?” Doug Wei glanced up at the man who said it.
strings.有人把饭盒底的一点饭渣抖在了木板角上。灰子窸窸窣窣地吃完，没走，就蹲在棚腿边上洗: Someone shook the last crumbs from a lunch tin onto the corner of the plank. Smoky ate them with a rustle and stayed, squatting by a prop leg to wash its face. From that day on, it came every day.
strings.有人提议：拆一节矿灯电池，用铁丝一碰就能打出火花，把刮下来的树皮烤一烤，再烧点开: Someone suggested breaking open a cap-lamp battery: short it with a wire and you get a spark, enough to toast the scraped bark and boil water to kill the germs. Something hot in the belly and a man lasts a few more days. Leon Tian went white: “Methane {var.ch4}. Have you all lost your minds?”
strings.有人提醒大家：听见了，不等于找到了。可那一晚，好几个人第一次睡着了。: Someone reminded them: hearing it doesn't mean they've found us. All the same, that night several of them slept for the first time.
strings.有人的伤口化脓了，红肿一圈圈往外蔓延，人烧得直打哆嗦。在井下，没有抗生素，这就是: A wound has gone septic; the red swelling spreads ring by ring, and the man is burning up, shaking all over. Underground, with no antibiotics, that's the end of him.
strings.有人第一个站了起来，抡起了镐把。: One man was first on his feet, swinging a pick handle.
strings.有人给贺小勇喂了一口水：“小贺，别乱说，好好歇着。”: Someone fed Eddie Ho a mouthful of water: “Eddie, don't talk nonsense. Rest.”
strings.有人腕上的电子表还在走——被困第{day}天了。黑暗里，有人在小声说话，有人在数: Someone's digital watch was still running—day {day} of being trapped. In the dark, low voices; someone counting his own heartbeat.
strings.有人说那钻机不一定是冲着这儿来的。巷道里又安静了下来，只剩远处的咚咚声。: Someone said the drill might not be aimed here at all. The roadway fell quiet again, nothing left but the distant thud.
strings.橡皮艇一趟一趟地往返，活着的人被抬上了井口：{survivors}。留在井下的：: The rubber boat went back and forth, trip after trip, carrying the living up to the pithead: {survivors}. Left underground: {dead}. The accident bulletin called it a “sudden inrush”. Those who lived got compensation, and no one ever brought up the hours before the water came.
strings.橡皮艇把人一趟一趟地运了出去：{survivors}。留在井下的：{dead}。: The rubber boat carried them out trip after trip: {survivors}. Left underground: {dead}. In the statements taken afterwards, every man told those days a little differently—who got on the boat first, who was left behind, and how he came to be left. The investigators wrote in their notebooks for a long time, then closed them and said: “What happened underground, let it end underground.” But of the men who came up, not one could ever settle it.
strings.正常是 0.04%。超过 3% 头疼气喘，超过 5% 意识模糊、干不了重活，超过: Normally 0.04%. Above 3%, headaches and gasping; above 5%, confusion and no strength for heavy work; above 7%, people collapse and can't be roused; at 9% it soon kills.
strings.正常空气是 20.9%。低于 18% 头晕乏力，低于 15% 判断力明显下降，低: Normal air is 20.9%. Below 18% you feel dizzy and weak; below 15% judgement goes; below 10% people collapse and can't be roused; below 7% it kills within minutes.
strings.每个人捧着一小袋葡萄糖水，一小口一小口地抿，谁也舍不得咽下去。: Each of them held a small pouch of glucose water, sipping in tiny mouthfuls, no one willing to swallow.
strings.每人约 700 千卡；可饿久了猛吃，可能出大事: About 700 kcal each; but after a long fast, eating hard can go badly wrong
strings.每人轮流吸几口: A few breaths each, taking turns
strings.每天平时照明用掉的灯时。: Lamp-hours burned each day for ordinary light.
strings.每天照明约 1.5 灯时，最省电；可长时间的黑暗会一点点把人压垮: About 1.5 lamp-hours of light a day, the least drain on the charge; but long darkness wears a man down by degrees
strings.每天照明约 3 灯时；黑着的时候多了，人心会慌: About 3 lamp-hours of light a day; more time in the dark, and nerves begin to fray
strings.每天照明约 9 灯时，电会很快用完: About 9 lamp-hours of light a day; the charge will run out fast
strings.气瓶还剩一百二十个压，够我一个来回，不够两个。: A hundred and twenty bar left in the tank. Enough for one round trip, not two.
strings.氧气……掉到十七了。大家……少说话。: Oxygen… down to seventeen. Everyone… talk less.
strings.氧气已经稀薄到让人站不起来了：有人瘫在地上，怎么叫都叫不醒。: The oxygen is now so thin that people can't stay on their feet: some lie slumped on the ground and can't be roused.
strings.水位 = 老空区来水（第一天最猛，之后每天衰减约 18%）− 地面排水（第二天起: Water level = inflow from the old workings (worst on the first day, then easing by about 18% a day) − pumping from the surface (more pumps are installed from day two, so the drainage rate rises every day). If the water reaches where you are, people soaking in it lose heat and strength, and in the worst case drown. Only when the water drops below the roof of the main roadway can the rescue team's rubber boats get in.
strings.水位降下去了，坡底的大巷露出了一道缝。远处传来突突的马达声，接着是一束晃动的灯光: The water had dropped; a slit of the main roadway showed at the bottom of the slope. A motor puttered in the distance, then a swaying light—the rescue team's rubber boat pushed through! It carries only two a trip, and a round trip takes over an hour. Who goes first?
strings.水壶里剩下的水，和接到的顶板淋水。脚下的积水不算——那是老空水，又酸又浑。: What's left in the water bottles, plus whatever you catch from the roof drips. The water at your feet doesn't count—that's old-workings water, sour and murky.
strings.水漫到了平台的下沿，还在涨。最多再过一夜，水就会淹到大家躺着的地方——伤员的腿动: The water had reached the lower edge of the platform and was still rising. One more night at most and it would reach where they lay—and the injured man's leg won't move. How do you get through tonight?
strings.水面上漂过来一个饭盒，卡在离岸七八米的一根坑木上，在矿灯下一沉一浮。推选一个人游: A lunch tin floated in and caught on a pit prop seven or eight metres from the bank, bobbing in the lamplight. Pick one man to swim out and bring it back.
strings.水面离你们待的平台还有多高（垂直距离）。降到 0 就淹到脚下了；回落到 11 米: How far the water surface is below your platform (vertically). At 0 it's at your feet; only when it drops back past 11 metres does the roof of the main roadway at the bottom of the slope clear the water so the rescue boats can get in.
strings.沉稳、话少，信老辈人的经验和规矩；遇事先看、先听、先闻；对年轻人严厉但心软；最怕: Steady and quiet; trusts the old hands' experience and the old rules. Looks, listens and smells before he acts. Hard on young men but soft-hearted. What he dreads most is being a burden.
strings.沉默、能忍、看人很准；习惯了被安排最差的活；不轻易信人，可谁对他好，他记一辈子；: Silent, enduring, a sharp judge of people; used to being handed the worst work. Slow to trust, but whoever treats him well, he remembers for life. When it counts, he's braver than any of them.
strings.没人再提这件事。树皮还是生着嚼。: No one brought it up again. The bark was still chewed raw.
strings.没人再说话，可每个人心里都记下了。: No one said anything more, but every man marked it.
strings.没人动。黑暗里的喊声，慢慢变成了抽泣。: No one moved. The shouting in the dark slowly turned to sobbing.
strings.没人理它。灰子在木板边上转了两圈，叼走了一粒掉在地上的饭渣。: No one paid it any mind. Smoky made two turns by the plank and carried off a crumb from the floor.
strings.没人说话。每个人都把耳朵贴在煤壁上，听了一整夜。: No one spoke. Every man pressed an ear to the coal wall and listened all night.
strings.没有人说话。有人在黑暗里低低地哭。: Nobody spoke. Someone wept quietly in the dark.
strings.没有热量，只是骗骗肚子: No calories—it only fools the belly
strings.没等到第二趟船: Never lived to see the second trip
strings.活着出去，把矿上瞒报透水征兆的真相交出去——哪怕连自己一起: Get out alive and hand over the truth about the hidden warning signs—even if it takes you down too
strings.活着出去，让这帮正式工把你当自己人: Get out alive, and make these company men accept him as one of their own
strings.活着回去见媳妇，别让矿关了、赔偿和工钱泡了汤: Get home alive to his wife—and don't let the mine be shut down and the compensation and back pay go up in smoke
strings.淹没段有多长、哪里顶板离水面还有缝、哪里有塌下来的支架挡路。潜水出去之前，必须先: How long the flooded stretch is, where there's still a gap between roof and water, where fallen supports block the way. You have to find out before anyone dives out.
strings.清点了一遍：七个人都在，贺小勇的腿断了，小满的手还在抖。坡下的黑水还在往上爬，矿: A head count: all seven are here. Eddie Ho's leg is broken; Manny's hands are still shaking. Below, the black water keeps climbing; in the lamplight, pit props and lumps of coal float on the surface. Three lunch tins, half a bag of biscuits, two packs of instant noodles and a few water bottles—that's everything you own. What first?
strings.潜出去的人在坡底另一头的大巷里，被一队正在架水泵的救护队员撞见了。地面连夜调来大: The man who dived out came up in the main roadway on the far side of the slope, right into a rescue crew rigging pumps. Through the night the surface brought in high-power submersible pumps and pumped at the low stretch; the rescue divers followed the scouted route and brought the rest out one by one. Those who lived to see the sky: {survivors}. Those who never saw this day: {dead}.
strings.火苗只窜起来一小会儿。烤焦的树皮又香又苦，烧开的水烫得人直吸气。: The flame flared only for a moment. The scorched bark was fragrant and bitter; the boiled water so hot they sucked in their breath.
strings.灯一亮，他看清了周围一张张熟悉的脸，慢慢安静了下来。: With the lamp lit, he made out the familiar faces around him and slowly went quiet.
strings.灯灭了。黑暗像水一样漫上来，有人在黑暗里一遍遍喊别人的名字，确认大家都还在。: The lamp went out. The dark rose like water, and someone called the others' names over and over, making sure they were all still there.
strings.灰子“吱”的一声钻进了煤帮的缝里，再也没出来。: With a squeak, Smoky darted into a crack in the coal wall and never came out again.
strings.灰子死在最高的那根棚梁上，蜷成一团，身子还是软的。谁也没说话——老辈人的话谁都记: Smoky died on the highest roof beam, curled into a ball, its body still soft. Nobody said a word—they all remembered what the old-timers said: where even a rat can't last, people won't last much longer.
strings.灰子被吃掉的那天夜里，有个老矿工一口都没碰，背过身去念叨了很久。后来有人说起这件: The night Smoky was eaten, one old miner wouldn't touch a bite; he turned his back and muttered to himself for a long time. Whenever anyone tells the story later, they add: in those days nobody was really human. They were just hunger.
strings.灰子钻进了尽头煤帮的一道裂缝，不见了。: Smoky slipped into a crack in the coal wall at the far end and was gone.
strings.煤帮后面有一道裂缝，丝丝地往外透着凉气。大家把脸凑过去，深深地吸了几口。: Behind the coal wall a crack hissed out cool air. They put their faces to it and drew deep breaths.
strings.煤没有一点热量；有人说嚼着能压住饿，也有人嚼出了肠梗阻: Coal has no calories at all; some say chewing it dulls hunger—and some chew their way into a bowel obstruction
strings.照医生说的，小口慢慢喝: Do as the doctor said: small sips, slowly
strings.照实回：下面的是罗小满，十七岁: Answer honestly: it's Manny Luo down here, seventeen
strings.爆炸过去了一天。巷道里弥漫着焦糊味和一股甜丝丝的怪味——是一氧化碳。活下来的人头: A day had passed since the explosion. The roadway reeked of scorching and a strange sweet smell—carbon monoxide. The survivors' heads ached too much to lift, their lips were blue, and their burns stung.
strings.王福山从胶靴筒里摸出打火机和半包烟，放在木板上：“我老糊涂了。”: Felix Wang fished the lighter and half a pack of cigarettes out of his boot and laid them on the plank: “I'm a foolish old man.”
strings.王福山和田立新把自己的饭盒揣回了怀里。木板上只剩下贺小勇的饭盒、半袋饼干和小满的: Felix Wang and Leon Tian tuck their lunch tins back inside their jackets. All that's left on the plank is Eddie Ho's tin, half a bag of biscuits and Manny's two packs of noodles—Manny didn't understand and had already put them out. James Hao's tin is nowhere to be found; he swears once and says nothing more.
strings.王福山咳了一整夜，咳得弯下腰去，嘴唇发紫。尘肺病人的肺本来就只剩一半能用，现在的: Felix Wang coughed all night, bent double, his lips blue. A man with black lung has only half a lung working at the best of times, and this air was too thick for him.
strings.王福山咳了几声，慢慢地说：“打偏了，说明他们在找。找的人还在，咱就有救。”: Felix Wang coughed a few times and said slowly: “A miss means they're looking. As long as they're looking, we've got a chance.”
strings.王福山在水边的煤帮上划了一道白印子。所有人每隔一会儿就去看一眼。: Felix Wang scored a white mark on the coal wall at the water's edge. Every so often someone went to look at it.
strings.王福山戴上自救器，大口喘了一阵，咳嗽总算停了。: Felix Wang put on the self-rescuer and gulped at it for a while; at last the coughing stopped.
strings.王福山把打火机凑到树皮底下，用手护着那一小簇火苗。: Felix Wang held the lighter under the bark, cupping the little flame with his hand.
strings.王福山把打火机扔进了坡下的黑水里。: Felix Wang threw the lighter into the black water below the slope.
strings.王福山抱住徒弟的上身，石磊按住他的腿，田立新数到三——贺小勇咬着毛巾闷叫了一声，: Felix Wang held his apprentice's shoulders, Larry Shi pinned the leg, Leon Tian counted to three—Eddie Ho bit down on a towel, gave a muffled cry and passed out. The bone was set and splinted with strips of pit prop, bound tight with bandage.
strings.王福山是被乔卫东绑在身上，从黑水底下带出去的——五十七岁的人，在水里死死闭着眼，: Felix Wang came out strapped to Wayne Qiao, dragged under the black water—a fifty-seven-year-old man with his eyes squeezed shut, clinging to the diver's belt and refusing to let go. The first thing he said at the pithead was: “Where's Eddie?”
strings.王福山没能上来。贺小勇后来说，师傅最后两天把自己那口饼干都偷偷塞给了他。王福山胶: Felix Wang didn't make it up. Eddie Ho said later that in the last two days his master had secretly slipped him his own share of biscuit. The lighter and the half pack of cigarettes from Felix Wang's boot stayed with Eddie Ho. He never smoked a single one.
strings.王福山活着出来了，徒弟没有。他把贺小勇的安全帽挂在自家窑洞的墙上，帽圈里的名字被: Felix Wang came out alive; his apprentice did not. He hung Eddie Ho's hard hat on the wall of his cave house, and rubbed the name inside the band until it shone. That winter his black lung went to stage two, and he never went underground again.
strings.王福山的事，后来矿上的老人们常常说起。说到最后，总是那句老辈人的话：井下的事，急: The old men at the mine still talk about Felix Wang. And they always end the same way, with the old saying: underground, you can't rush things.
strings.王福山葬在了他挖了三十六年煤的那座山的山脚下，坟头朝着井口。老伴说，这下好了，他: Felix Wang is buried at the foot of the mountain he dug coal under for thirty-six years, his grave facing the pithead. His wife said, well, that's it then—he never has to go down again.
strings.王福山说，当年老辈人遇上透水，就是把自己绑在棚子上熬过来的。每个人都解下皮带，把: Felix Wang said that when the old-timers met a flood, they lashed themselves to the props and rode it out. Every man took off his belt and tied himself under a roof beam. Doug Wei climbed up first and lashed Eddie Ho to the highest one.
strings.王福山躲在坡下抽完了一根烟，手一直在抖。: Felix Wang hid below the slope and smoked a whole cigarette, his hand shaking the whole time.
strings.现在就拆，把他拖过来: Break it open now and drag him over
strings.班长的事，大家有权知道: The men have a right to know about the crew boss
strings.瓦斯 {var.ch4}……坡下也许没那么浓: Methane {var.ch4}… maybe it's thinner down the slope
strings.瓦斯从老空区不断渗出，比空气轻，会积在上山巷道的顶部。浓度超过 1% 严禁任何火: Methane seeps steadily out of the old workings. It is lighter than air and collects along the roof of the rise. Above 1%, no spark of any kind is allowed; where it pools at 5–16%, a flame will set it off.
strings.瓦斯便携仪“嘀嘀嘀”地尖叫起来：瓦斯 {var.ch4}，超限了。上山是条死头巷: The handheld detector screamed—methane {var.ch4}, over the limit. The rise is a dead end, and methane is lighter than air; it all gathers along the roof.
strings.瓦斯便携仪的读数。超过 1% 必须停止一切作业、严禁火花；巷道顶上局部积到 5%: The reading on the handheld methane detector. Above 1%, all work must stop and no sparks are allowed; where it pools at 5–16% along the roof, a flame will set it off.
strings.瓦斯少一些；可坡下离水近，二氧化碳更浓: Less methane; but down by the water the carbon dioxide is thicker
strings.用尿冲洗伤口——老辈人的土法子: Wash the wound with urine—an old-timers' folk remedy
strings.用扳手和镐拆下被砸扁的阀门，掏净管口里的煤泥，再把管头接好。要打着灯干，很费技术: Take off the flattened valve with a wrench and a pick, dig the slurry out of the pipe end and fit a new connection. It has to be done by lamplight and takes real skill. Even when it's done there may be no air: that depends on whether the compressor on the surface is running, and whether the stretch under the water is intact.
strings.用掉 1 份急救用品: Use up 1 unit of first aid
strings.用掉 1 台自救器，能让最虚的人缓一口气: Use up 1 self-rescuer; the weakest man gets a breather
strings.用掉 1.5 升干净的水: Use up 1.5 L of clean water
strings.用王福山的打火机，火小一点: Use Felix Wang's lighter—a smaller flame
strings.用碘伏和干净的水反复冲洗、重新包扎: Flush it over and over with iodine and clean water, then re-dress it
strings.用镐把敲压风管和钢轨：每隔一刻钟敲一轮“三长两短”，地面上有人拿着仪器在听。敲得: Beat the air line and the rails with a pick handle: every quarter of an hour, a round of “three long, two short”. Someone on the surface is listening with instruments. The steadier and longer you knock, the surer the rescuers are of where you are, and the better aimed the borehole. It costs no lamp, but it costs strength—and air.
strings.用风筒布往下扇，把顶上的瓦斯搅散: Fan down with duct cloth to break up the methane along the roof
strings.田立新一个人抱着管子拆了一下午，手上全是煤泥。: Leon Tian spends the whole afternoon alone, arms round the pipe, taking it apart; his hands are covered in coal slurry.
strings.田立新一把抢回了本子：“安监站的东西，你少管。”: Leon Tian snatches the notebook back: “The safety station's business. Keep out of it.”
strings.田立新回到了安监站，第二年提了副站长。他开出来的罚单比谁都多，查到“挂汗”“出水: Leon Tian went back to the safety station and made deputy chief the following year. He wrote more fines than anyone; any face that was “sweating” or seeping water, he shut down on the spot, and no one could talk him out of it. Only he knew why.
strings.田立新在调查组面前把一切都说了，连同那两千块钱。他被判了缓刑，丢了安监站的饭碗。: Leon Tian told the investigators everything, including the two thousand yuan. He got a suspended sentence and lost his job at the safety station. Later he taught at a safety training school, and whenever he came to the chapter on hazard inspection he would stop for a moment: “I tore out a page once.”
strings.田立新把扳手放下了，什么也没说。: Leon Tian puts the wrench down and says nothing.
strings.田立新接过笔，一笔一画写下了他知道的一切：隐患记录、被撕掉的那一页、矿长塞来的两: Leon Tian takes the pen and writes it all down, stroke by stroke, everything he knows: the hazard inspection log, the torn-out page, the two thousand yuan the mine manager pressed on him. When he finishes, his hand will not stop shaking.
strings.田立新没能上来。他绑在钻杆上的那张纸，后来成了事故调查报告里编号第一的证据，矿长: Leon Tian didn't make it up. The paper he tied to the drill rod became Exhibit One in the accident investigation, and the mine manager went to prison. On the day of the trial there was an empty seat in the front row of the public gallery, with a white safety-station hard hat on it.
strings.田立新用劈开的坑木条和两根皮带给他做了夹板。: Leon Tian makes him a splint from a split pit prop and two belts.
strings.田立新的名字后来出现在一份内部通报里，只有一行。知道那一行背后是什么的人，都没再: Leon Tian's name later appeared in an internal bulletin, a single line. The people who knew what lay behind that line never brought it up again.
strings.田立新的塑封小本子是在他贴身的口袋里找到的，最新的那一页被撕掉了。调查组的人对着: Leon Tian's laminated notebook was found in an inside pocket, its latest page torn out. The investigators looked at that ragged edge for a long time, and in the end filed the notebook under “personal effects” rather than “evidence”.
strings.田立新蹲在压风管旁边，用扳手敲了敲管壁，又把耳朵贴上去听了很久：“阀门砸扁了，管: Leon Tian crouches by the compressed-air line, taps the pipe wall with a wrench, then puts his ear to it for a long time: “The valve's flattened and the pipe end is packed solid. If we can take it apart and join it up, the moment they start the compressor on the surface, fresh air comes down to us—provided the stretch under the water isn't broken.”
strings.电很快就会用光；可这几分钟，所有人都会想起井上的日子: The charge will be gone soon; but for these few minutes, everyone remembers the days above ground
strings.留住一条命；可他心里那团火，压不住多久: Saves his life; but the fire in him can be held down only so long
strings.留着那两格电，等最难熬的时候用；也替他留着这个秘密: Save those two bars of charge for the worst of it; and keep his secret for him
strings.留着，夜里自己偷偷吃: Keep it, and eat it in secret at night
strings.直爽、冲动、好面子，认准了就往前冲；崇拜班长；一想到媳妇就红眼眶，嘴上死不承认。: Straightforward, impulsive, proud; once he's made up his mind he charges ahead. Idolises the crew boss. Gets red-eyed whenever he thinks of his wife, and will never admit it.
strings.省下一点吃的；韦德贵会记恨，别人看了也会寒心: Saves a little food; Doug Wei will hold it against you, and the others will turn cold
strings.省下急救用品，效果看田立新的手艺: Saves the first-aid kit; how well it goes depends on Leon Tian's skill
strings.省下的口粮给干活的人；王福山不会原谅你: The rations you save go to the men who work; Felix Wang will never forgive you
strings.省下这口气；他能不能撑到那时候，谁也说不准: Save that breath; whether he lasts that long, nobody can say
strings.省着力气，每到整点敲一轮: Save your strength and knock a round on the hour
strings.省矿山救护总队的队员，当过五年海军潜水兵，是队里唯一能背着气瓶在矿井水里潜的人。: A member of the Provincial Mine Rescue Corps who spent five years as a navy diver; the only man in the corps who can dive in mine water with a tank on his back. Right now he is at the rescue command post at the pithead, tanks filled, fins at his feet, waiting for someone to tell him where to dive.
strings.真相会让班长威信扫地: The truth will cost the crew boss his standing
strings.睡着了也不会滑进水里，泡水和溺水的危险小得多；可吊一夜，人会累垮: Asleep, nobody slides into the water, and the risk of soaking and drowning is far smaller; but a night hanging there breaks a man
strings.石磊升井三个月后，儿子出生了，小名叫“井生”。矿没关，赔偿和工钱一分没少。半年后: Three months after Larry Shi came up, his son was born; at home they call him Jingsheng—“born of the shaft”. The mine stayed open, and every yuan of compensation and wages was paid. Six months later he went back underground. There are twenty years left on the mortgage for the flat in town.
strings.石磊后来很少回福源。有人在太原的工地上见过他，比以前瘦了，话也少了。别人问起井下: Larry Shi rarely went back to Fuyuan. Someone saw him on a building site in Taiyuan: thinner than before, and quieter. When people asked about those days underground, he just smiled and said he'd long forgotten.
strings.石磊哥，你说外头这会儿是白天还是晚上？: Brother Larry Shi, do you reckon it's day or night up there now?
strings.石磊是被赶到坡下去的，怀里还揣着那只刻着“郝”字的饭盒。救护队找到他的时候，饭盒: Larry Shi was driven down the slope with the lunch tin marked “Hao” still inside his jacket. When the rescue team found him, the tin was empty, its lid shut tight. His wife never would believe that his own people had sent him down there.
strings.石磊的儿子是在他头七那天出生的，媳妇给孩子取名石念。县城那套房子的首付，后来是用: Larry Shi's son was born on the seventh day after his death. His wife named the boy Shi Nian—“remembrance”. The deposit on the flat in town was paid with the compensation money in the end; she moved in alone with the baby. Their wedding photo hangs in the living room, and in it he is grinning wide enough to show a crooked tooth.
strings.矿灯全灭以后过了几天。: How many days since the last cap lamp died.
strings.矿灯已经暗下去好几盏了。田立新把所有的灯挨个看了一遍：剩下的电加起来，还能让一盏: Several cap lamps have dimmed out already. Leon Tian goes through every one of them: put together, the charge left will keep a single lamp burning {res.lamp}. The days ahead—do you live them in light, or in the dark?
strings.矿被关了，工钱拖了一年才结清。石磊带着媳妇和刚满月的儿子去了太原，在工地上开塔吊: The mine was shut down, and it took a year to get the back pay. Larry Shi took his wife and their one-month-old son to Taiyuan and drove a tower crane on building sites, forty metres up with nothing above him but sky. He said he never wanted to go underground again as long as he lived.
strings.矿长、田立新、也许还有班长，都会被追责；石磊会恨你: The mine manager, Leon Tian, maybe the crew boss too—they will all be held to account; and Larry Shi will hate you
strings.砖墙拆开的时候，赵存柱已经坐不起来了。几个人把他从洞里拖出来，平放在木板上。他睁: When the brick wall is opened, Charlie Zhao cannot even sit up. They drag him out through the hole and lay him flat on a plank. He opens his eyes, looks round at them and smiles: “So many… a crowd's a good thing.”
strings.私下找他要一口: Ask him for a mouthful in private
strings.私藏的吃的会被充公，石磊会记恨你: The food you hoarded goes into the common pool, and Larry Shi will hold it against you
strings.稳妥，但被压的人要多受一阵罪: Safe, but the man pinned down suffers longer
strings.空气按“气囊”计算：被水封住的巷道里能用的空气，随水位涨落变化（水面每涨 1 米: The air is modelled as a pocket: the breathable air left in a roadway sealed off by water, which shrinks and grows as the water rises and falls (each metre of rise costs about 60 cubic metres). A person at rest uses about 0.38 cubic metres of oxygen a day, roughly double that when working, and breathes out carbon dioxide at about 85% of the oxygen used. The old workings also seep carbon dioxide (most in the first few days, and the amount differs from game to game), and the slow oxidation of the coal walls eats oxygen too. Oxygen below 17% or carbon dioxide above 3% starts to do harm, and men with black lung feel it sooner; at 5% carbon dioxide nobody can manage heavy work, at 7% (or with oxygen down to 10%) people collapse, and at 9% (or oxygen at 7%) it kills outright. Breaking open the brick seal at the end would join on the air of an old roadway (about 150 cubic metres), but the methane and carbon dioxide trapped behind it for years would pour out all at once.
strings.第{day}天，救护队员的头灯照进 2 号上山的时候，没有一个人敢睁眼——矿灯早: On day {day}, when the rescuers' headlamps reach into the No. 2 Rise, nobody dares open his eyes—the cap lamps died long ago, and they have been in the black longer than they can say. The rescuers blindfold each of them with black cloth and carry them onto the rubber boats: {survivors}. Those who did not live to see this light: {dead}. The doctors say eyes kept that long in the dark will take light again in a few days; but some of them never slept with the light off again.
strings.第二天，{actor} 和石磊谁也没提昨晚的事。: The next day, neither {actor} nor Larry Shi mentions the night before.
strings.第二趟船晚了将近两个钟头——大巷里塌了一段顶，艇过不来。等船终于回来，{acto: The second boat is nearly two hours late—part of the roof has come down in the main roadway and the boat can't get through. By the time it finally comes back, {actor} has stopped breathing.
strings.第十四天，水泵终于把坡底的水抽下去了一截。救护队员蹚着齐胸深的水摸了进来，矿灯照: Day fourteen. The pumps have finally pulled the water at the bottom of the slope down a little. The rescuers wade in through chest-deep water, feeling their way; when their lamps reach the end of the roadway they stand there stunned for a long time. Carried out: {survivors}. Those who did not live to see this day: {dead}.
strings.等他清醒了再问: Wait until he's clear-headed, then ask
strings.等导向绳搓好、水再退一点再说: Wait until the guide rope is twisted and the water has dropped a little more
strings.管他呢，敞开喝: To hell with it—drink your fill
strings.管头接上的一瞬间，“嘶——”的一声，一股凉风扑到脸上。所有人都把脸凑了过去，大口: The moment the end is connected there's a hiss—and a cool breeze on their faces. Everyone crowds in and gulps at it.
strings.管头接好了，阀门一拧开，涌出来的不是风，是一股带着煤泥的黑水——压风管在水下的某: The end is connected, the valve opened—and what gushes out isn't air but black water full of coal slurry. Somewhere under the water, the air line is broken.
strings.管子接好了，里面却一点风也没有。田立新把耳朵贴在管壁上听了很久：管子是通的，只是: The line is connected, but nothing comes out. Leon Tian presses his ear to the pipe and listens for a long time: the line is clear; the compressor on the surface just isn't running yet.
strings.纸条上写了几行字：“我们 {aliveCount} 人在 2 号上山，有人腿断，: A few lines are written on the paper: “{aliveCount} of us in the No. 2 Rise. One man's leg is broken. Low on oxygen. Need air, water, medicine, urgently.” When the drill rod is pulled up, several of them burst into tears.
strings.纸条上只有一行字：“我们都还活着。”: There is only one line on the paper: “We're all still alive.”
strings.给它留点渣——老规矩: Leave it a few crumbs—the old rule
strings.给干重活、要冒险的人: For the men doing the heavy work and taking the risks
strings.给班长留面子，可小贺心里会凉: Spares the crew boss's face, but it turns Eddie Ho cold
strings.给贺小勇，他伤得最重: Give it to Eddie Ho—he's hurt the worst
strings.绳子突然乱抖起来。大家拼命往回拽，把 {actor} 从水里拖了上来——人已经发: Suddenly the rope jerks wildly. They haul on it for all they're worth and drag {actor} out of the water—already blue, {actor.he} lies on the ground retching black water for a long time before {actor.he} can breathe.
strings.绳子那头猛地乱抖起来。乔卫东把人拖回来的时候，面罩歪在一边，{actor} 已经: The rope jerks wildly. When Wayne Qiao drags the man back, his mask is knocked askew and {actor} has stopped breathing.
strings.缝越掏越窄，最后只剩一根指头粗。灰子过得去，人过不去。: The gap gets narrower the more they dig, until it is no wider than a finger. Smoky can get through. A man cannot.
strings.老实、认真、胆小，疼得厉害也只是咬着嘴唇；总觉得是自己没拦住大家。: Honest, conscientious, timid; even in terrible pain he only bites his lip. He keeps thinking it's his fault he didn't stop them.
strings.老矿工见过这种事: An old miner has seen this before
strings.老空区每天渗进来的二氧化碳（百分点），每局不同。: Carbon dioxide seeping in from the old workings each day (percentage points); it differs from game to game.
strings.老辈人说，井下有老鼠的地方就有活路。这一晚，大家睡得踏实了一点。: The old-timers say that where there are rats underground there is a way to live. That night, everyone sleeps a little easier.
strings.老辈人说，井下没药的时候，就是这么干的。: The old-timers say that is how it was done underground when there was no medicine.
strings.老鼠还在，说明这里的空气还撑得住: The rat is still here, so the air here still holds out
strings.胆小、机灵、记吃；谁给过它吃的，它就敢蹲在谁的胶靴边上。: Timid, quick-witted, never forgets a meal; whoever has fed it, it will dare to sit by their boots.
strings.能把巷道里的情况先告诉救护队；可留在后面的人，要多等一个多钟头: Tells the rescue team what the roadway is like first; but the men left behind wait more than another hour
strings.能救一条命，老巷道的空气也能和这边连成一片，以后空气更耐用；可墙一开，里面憋了多: Saves a life, and the air in the old roadway joins on to this one, so the air lasts longer after that; but the moment the wall comes down, the methane and carbon dioxide pent up there for years pour out at once—and there is one more mouth, one more pair of lungs
strings.能让他顶过最难熬的几个钟头: Gets him through the worst few hours
strings.能走的先走，给后面的人带路: Those who can walk go first, to lead the way for the others
strings.能顶几个灯时；可手机不防爆，瓦斯越高，亮一下屏都是在赌: Buys a few lamp-hours; but a phone is not explosion-proof, and the thicker the methane, the more of a gamble it is to light the screen even once
strings.腰上拴着绳子顺坡摸到水边，往水里探：淹没段有多长，顶板离水面还有没有缝，哪儿有塌: Go down the slope to the water's edge with a rope round your waist and feel your way into the water: how long is the flooded stretch, is there still a gap between roof and water, where do fallen supports block the way? The water's edge is where the carbon dioxide is thickest, and the footing is slick; anything could happen.
strings.腼腆、嘴甜、手脚勤快，怕被人嫌弃，抢着干活；一害怕就不停地说话；把韦德贵当亲叔叔: Shy, sweet-talking, quick to pitch in; afraid of being thought a nuisance, so he grabs every job. When he's scared he talks nonstop. He treats Doug Wei like an uncle and Larry Shi like a big brother.
strings.腿断了的人在这儿撑不了几天；可他没潜过水，在黑水里一慌，就可能把面罩扯掉: A man with a broken leg will not last long here; but he has never dived, and one panic in the black water could have him tearing his mask off
strings.自救器就这么几台: There are only so many self-rescuers
strings.自救器的口具塞进嘴里，那人大口吸了几下，脸色慢慢缓了过来。: The mouthpiece of the self-rescuer is pushed into his mouth; the man takes several deep pulls and the colour slowly comes back to his face.
strings.舀起坡下的积水，在饭盒里放一夜让煤泥沉下去，再用毛巾和风筒布滤几遍。能弄到不少水: Scoop up water from the bottom of the slope, leave it in a lunch tin overnight so the slurry settles, then strain it a few times through towels and duct cloth. You get plenty, but old-workings water is sour and tastes of rust, and even filtered it can give you the runs.
strings.药片被碾碎了，和着水一点点喂了下去。: The tablets are crushed and fed to him little by little with water.
strings.被困第{day}天，你们被一个个扶上了井口：{survivors}。没能上来的：: On day {day} underground, you are helped up to the pithead one by one: {survivors}. Those who did not come up: {dead}. A man with his left hand wrapped in gauze pushes to the front and picks you out one by one—Charlie Zhao. After he crawled out of the main roadway, the rescuers went where he said and found four more men high in the old 1201 return airway, one of them Benny Zhao. In the accident bulletin that followed, the list of the saved was one line longer than the original.
strings.被困第{day}天，最后一个人被扶出罐笼的时候，井口围着的人群一下子炸开了锅。家: On day {day} underground, when the last man is helped out of the cage, the crowd round the pithead erupts. The families weep and shout, picking out their own one by one: {survivors}—not one missing. The doctors said afterwards that you did not survive on luck, but on every mouthful of water and every breath shared out to each man.
strings.要拆掉一节电池（矿灯电量 −4）；瓦斯越浓越危险: Requires taking out a battery cell (lamp charge -4); the thicker the methane, the more dangerous
strings.要是我出不去，你们莫跟我娘说我是在井下没的。就说……就说是出车祸。: If I don't get out, don't tell my mum I died down a mine. Tell her… tell her it was a car crash.
strings.让他先带最虚弱的那个人出去: Have him take the weakest man out first
strings.让他先把贺小勇带出去: Have him take Eddie Ho out first
strings.让他去，给他最亮的那盏灯和一台自救器: Send him, with the brightest lamp and a self-rescuer
strings.让他家里人知道他还活着: Let his family know he is still alive
strings.让他把手机当手电用，省下矿灯: Have him use the phone as a torch and save the cap lamps
strings.让他留下来，跟大家一起等船: Have him stay and wait for the boat with the others
strings.让他给大家看看家里的照片，放一首歌: Let him show everyone photos from home and play a song
strings.让他自己缓过来: Let him come round on his own
strings.让他马上回去，把这边的情况报上去: Send him straight back to report what is happening here
strings.让地面尽快确定你们的位置；代价是一整夜的力气和空气: Gets the surface to fix your position as fast as it can; the cost is a whole night's strength and air
strings.让地面知道你们是谁、在哪: Let the surface know who you are and where you are
strings.让地面知道这边的情况: Let the surface know what is happening here
strings.让外面知道这场事故是怎么来的；田立新收钱的事也会一起抖出来，石磊怕矿一关、赔偿就: Lets the outside know how this disaster came about; the money Leon Tian took comes out with it, and Larry Shi is afraid that if the mine is shut the compensation goes up in smoke
strings.让徒弟贺小勇活着出去: Get his apprentice Eddie Ho out alive
strings.让田立新慢慢弄，别耽误找水找吃的: Let Leon Tian take his time, and do not hold up the search for water and food
strings.让郝建军当面说清楚: Make James Hao say it to your face
strings.说出十年前在贵州潜水逃生的事，然后下水: Tell the story of the Guizhou dive ten years ago, then go into the water
strings.说话很轻，喘着气，一句话分好几截说。: Speaks softly, out of breath, each sentence broken into pieces.
strings.请郝建军把话说清楚: Ask James Hao to come clean
strings.谁也没再说话。黑暗里只剩下一片粗重的喘气声。: Nobody speaks again. In the dark there is nothing but heavy breathing.
strings.谁也没去碰那道墙。墙那边的人喊了一夜，嗓子喊哑了，就改成敲；敲到后来，隔很久才响: Nobody touches the wall. On the far side they shout all night; when their voices give out they switch to knocking, and the knocks come further and further apart. By daylight there is nothing left to hear.
strings.谁头晕、谁心慌，先说。别硬扛。: Anyone dizzy, anyone's heart racing—say so. Don't tough it out.
strings.谁最撑不住谁先走；可越虚的人，在水底下越容易出事: The weakest go first; but the weaker a man is, the more easily it goes wrong under the water
strings.调查报告里“违法使用未成年人下井”那一行，写的就是罗小满。外包队老板被抓了，矿上: The line in the investigation report about “illegally employing a minor underground” was about Manny Luo. The contractor was arrested and the mine paid compensation. He went home to Bijie and learned car repair at the vocational school in his township. Every year at the end of March he phones the men he knew underground, one by one. They never say much; he just wants to hear that they're still there.
strings.谨慎、讲规程、爱较真，骨子里胆小；内疚的时候会拼命干活；不太会说软话。: Careful, a stickler for the rules, timid at heart; when he feels guilty he works himself to the bone. Not good at saying anything kind.
strings.贵州人，跟着老乡在外包队干了三年，干的是正式工不愿干的活：清浮煤、扛料、打杂。工: From Guizhou; he's spent three years in a contract crew with men from his home county, doing the jobs the company men won't touch: clearing loose coal, carrying supplies, odd jobs. His pay is a notch below theirs, and he can't eat in the canteen. The crew usually calls him “the contract guy” and rarely uses his name. Something iron in the water gashed his calf.
strings.贵州口音，话很少，爱说“要得”“莫慌”，被逼急了才冷冷地顶一句。: A Guizhou accent; says very little. Fond of “All right” and “Don't panic.” Only when pushed too far does he answer back, coldly.
strings.贵州毕节人，跟着老乡韦德贵出来，在外包队干了四个月：推车、扛料、清浮煤。工牌上写: From Bijie in Guizhou; he came north with Doug Wei, a man from his home county, and has worked four months in the contract crew—pushing tubs, carrying supplies, clearing loose coal. His work badge says “George Luo, 21”, but everyone calls him Manny. Small and skinny, with fuzz on his upper lip that has never seen a razor. He was at the face when the water broke in, and Doug Wei hauled him up the slope with one hand. Good with his hands; back home he helped his mother weave bamboo baskets.
strings.贵州那口小煤窑的事，后来大家都知道了，没人再说什么。韦德贵回了老家。第二年清明，: Eventually everyone heard about the little pit in Guizhou, and no one said anything. Doug Wei went home. At Qingming the next year he visited his cousin's grave for the first time, and sat in front of it all day.
strings.费不了几口吃的；老辈人说，耗子在，气就在: Costs hardly a bite of food; the old-timers say that while the rat is here, the air is here
strings.费力气、费灯，碰运气（矿灯电量 −1）: Costs strength and lamp, and it is a gamble (lamp charge -1)
strings.费力气也费空气，可地面越早找准你们越好: Costs strength and air, but the sooner the surface pinpoints you the better
strings.费力气，但能帮地面校准位置: Costs strength, but it helps the surface fix your position
strings.费力气，但能稳住他: Costs strength, but it steadies him
strings.费力气，碰运气: Costs strength, and it is a gamble
strings.贺小勇发着低烧，迷迷糊糊地一直念叨：“郝哥……迎头挂汗了……煤壁发凉……我说了要: Eddie Ho is running a low fever and keeps muttering, half out of it: “Brother Hao… the face was sweating… the coal was cold… I said we had to stop…” The roadway goes quiet at once, and every eye turns to James Hao.
strings.贺小勇右小腿的伤口里露着骨头茬，腿肿得发亮，一碰就疼得浑身发抖，胸口也疼得只能小: Bone pokes out of the wound in Eddie Ho's right shin; the leg is swollen and shiny, and the lightest touch sets him shaking with pain. His chest hurts so much he can only take tiny breaths. Leon Tian says the bone has to be set, dressed and splinted, or the wound will go bad and he'll lose the leg—and maybe more. There's only enough in the first-aid kit to do this once.
strings.贺小勇拉住领头人 {leader} 的袖子，喘着气说：“别再给我分吃的了……我腿: Eddie Ho catches at the sleeve of {leader} and says, gasping: “Stop giving me food… my leg is broken, I cannot do anything… leave it for the men who can work.”
strings.贺小勇是被乔卫东绑在身上，从黑水底下拖出去的。那条腿最后还是截到了膝盖。他后来在: Eddie Ho was dragged out under the black water, strapped to Wayne Qiao. In the end the leg was taken off at the knee. Later he answered phones in the mine's dispatch room, and every time he heard the word “inrush”, the hand holding the receiver shook.
strings.贺小勇没说什么，只是把脸转向了煤帮。王福山盯着说“等”的人看了很久。: Eddie Ho says nothing; he only turns his face to the coal wall. Felix Wang stares a long time at the man who said “wait”.
strings.贺小勇的右腿保住了，只是短了一截，走路一瘸一拐。他没再下井，在县里的安全培训中心: Eddie Ho kept his right leg, though it ended up shorter and he walks with a limp. He never went underground again and became an instructor at the county safety training centre. To every new intake of miners, the first thing he says is: “When the coal sweats, you stop. Whoever tells you otherwise, you stop.”
strings.贺小勇的烧退了些，人也清醒了。他看着郝建军，声音很轻：“郝哥……那天的事，还是你: Eddie Ho's fever has eased and his head is clearer. He looks at James Hao, his voice very soft: “Brother Hao… the thing that day, better you tell it yourself.”
strings.贺小勇的瓦斯便携仪后来交给了事故调查组，里面存着被困那几天的每一个读数。调查组的: Eddie Ho's methane detector went to the accident investigators. It held every reading from the days they were trapped. The investigators said it was the most complete record of conditions underground they had ever seen. His name is carved on the memorial at the mine gate.
strings.贺小勇那份吃的被分了出去。他笑了笑，说这样挺好。: Eddie Ho's share is handed out. He smiles and says that is good.
strings.赵存柱从大巷的水里爬出去的时候，救护队员差点没认出那是个人。他在医院里躺了二十天: When Charlie Zhao crawled out of the water in the main roadway, the rescuers barely recognised him as a man. He spent twenty days in hospital and lost two fingers on his left hand. Benny and the other three were found exactly where he said they'd be. Later the two brothers opened a little shop at the edge of the village selling cigarettes, liquor—and cap-lamp batteries.
strings.赵存柱咬着自救器的口具，腰上拴着一根风筒布条，一步一步走进了黑水。大家守着水面，: Charlie Zhao bites down on the mouthpiece of a self-rescuer, a strip of duct cloth tied round his waist, and walks step by step into the black water. They keep watch on the surface and wait a long, long time.
strings.赵存柱把那只烂手往怀里一揣，对着坡下的黑水看了很久：“大巷那段我熟——四百米，两: Charlie Zhao tucks the ruined hand inside his jacket and looks a long time at the black water below the slope: “I know that stretch of the main roadway—four hundred metres, two bends, the lowest point at the mouth of No. 3 crosscut. I will swim through, tell them up top that Benny and the others are in the old return airway, and tell them where you are.” He coughs until he cannot straighten up, but his eyes are frighteningly bright.
strings.赵存柱接过灯，冲大家点了点头，什么也没说。: Charlie Zhao takes the lamp, nods to them all and says nothing.
strings.赵存柱是被抬上井的，一上来就抓着救护队员的袖子问存旺。存旺他们是在老回风巷里找到: Charlie Zhao was carried up the shaft and grabbed a rescuer's sleeve the moment he came out, asking for Benny. Benny's group was found in the old return airway: two alive, two not. Missing two fingers, he later opened a repair shop in the village, with that day's hard hat hanging on the wall.
strings.赵存柱没能回家。他的遗物里只有一盏摔裂了的矿灯，和一张塑封的全家福——照片上，他: Charlie Zhao never made it home. All he left was a cracked cap lamp and a laminated family photo: he and Benny crouching side by side outside their cave house, grinning the same goofy grin. Benny was found later in the old return airway—two days too late.
strings.赵存柱点了点头，坐回去接着敲管子。敲两下，就扭头看一眼坡下的水。: Charlie Zhao nods, sits back down and goes on knocking the pipe. Two knocks, then a look back at the water at the bottom of the slope.
strings.趁还有力气，把坑木、木板和煤袋子往上垒（水面距离 +0.5 米），人会累得够呛: Use your strength while you have it to stack pit props, planks and coal sacks (water gap +0.5 m). Everyone will be worn out
strings.越是这样，越要抓紧干活、敲管子: All the more reason to keep working and knocking the pipe
strings.跟着老鼠去找缝隙，也许那里透风: Follow the rat to the crack. Maybe there's air through there
strings.身体最好的几个人先上了艇。留下的人看着他们，谁也没有说话。: The fittest few got on the boat first. Those left behind watched them. Nobody said a word.
strings.躲到坡下，偷偷点一根: Hide down the slope and sneak a cigarette
strings.过了两个多钟头，管子里又“嘶”地响了起来。有人长长地出了一口气。: After more than two hours the pipe hissed again. Someone let out a long breath.
strings.还给他，什么也不问: Give it back to him and ask nothing
strings.还能再往上躲半米（水面距离 +0.4 米），可所有人挤在一起，喘气更费劲: You could still get half a metre higher (water gap +0.4 m), but packed in together, everyone finds it harder to breathe
strings.这只手不顶事了，另一只还行。: This hand's no good any more. The other one still works.
strings.这是他的名字、他的命，让他自己定: It's his name, his life—let him decide
strings.这根棚子吃劲了。递根木头过来。: This set's taking the load. Pass me a timber.
strings.这绳子我编得紧，一米一个疙瘩，摸黑也数得清。: I'm twisting this rope tight. A knot every metre—you can count them in the dark.
strings.进度慢，可不耽误别的活: Slow going, but it doesn't hold up other work
strings.透水前两个钟头，迎头煤壁就“挂汗”了，隐隐有“嘶嘶”的水声，煤壁摸着发凉——这是: Two hours before the inrush, the coal at the face was already “sweating”; there was a faint hiss of water, and the coal felt cold to the touch—the classic warning signs, and the regulations say to stop work and pull everyone out. Eddie Ho said to stop right then. But the crew was thirty metres short of its footage for the month, and every metre short meant a metre's pay docked for all of them, so you said, “One more round of shots, then we go.” That round broke into the old workings.
strings.那一茬炮的事，郝建军在调查组面前又说了一遍，一个字没改。违章指挥，撤职，罚款，留: James Hao told the investigators about that last round again, word for word. Ordering work in breach of regulations: dismissed, fined, kept on at the mine on probation. Later he drove a loader in the coal yard on the surface, and on night shifts he would often stand alone smoking, looking up at the headframe, half the night through.
strings.那一页的事井下的人都知道了，可事故报告上一个字也没有。田立新调去了邻县的矿，再没: Everyone who was down there knew about the page, but the accident report never mentioned it. Leon Tian transferred to a mine in the next county and never came back to Fuyuan. When men from those days ran into him in the street, he would duck his head and cross to the other side.
strings.那不一定是冲着这儿来的，别白费劲: It may not be aimed at us. Don't waste your strength
strings.那两根蜡烛谁都看见了；问出来，就得有人担这个事: Everyone saw those two candles; if it comes out, someone has to answer for it
strings.那天……我要是再喊大声一点就好了。: That day… if only I'd shouted louder.
strings.那年冬天，班里的人凑钱给韦德贵寄了一箱山西老陈醋，箱子上用记号笔写着：德贵收。他: That winter the crew chipped in and sent Doug Wei a crate of aged Shanxi vinegar, with “For Doug” written on the box in marker pen. He couldn't bring himself to open it and kept it on the cabinet in the front room. His name was on the mine's list for a permanent contract. He didn't take it—two floods, he said, were enough for one life.
strings.那是你自己带的口粮；被人发现就说不清了: That's your own ration; if it's found on you, you'll never explain it away
strings.郝哥……我不怪你。我就是……想回家。: Brother Hao… I don't blame you. I just… want to go home.
strings.郝建军包里的一卷绷带、几块纱布和一小瓶碘伏。: A roll of bandage, a few gauze pads and a small bottle of iodine from James Hao's bag.
strings.郝建军升井后当了半年“救人的班长”，县电视台来采访过两回，奖金他分给了全班。每到: For half a year after he came up, James Hao was “the crew boss who saved his men”. The county TV station interviewed him twice, and he split the reward among the crew. Every month-end, when the footage was reported, he sat in the dispatch room for a long time—and he never again said “one more round”.
strings.郝建军张了张嘴，什么也没说。贺小勇闭上了眼睛。: James Hao opened his mouth and said nothing. Eddie Ho shut his eyes.
strings.郝建军是被自己带了九年的班赶到坡下去的。救护队后来在水边的一根棚腿上找到了他——: James Hao was driven down the slope by the crew he had led for nine years. The rescue team found him later at the water's edge, strapped to a prop with his own belt, already cold. Not one man in the crew would sign the page of the investigation report that covered him.
strings.郝建军沉默了很久，最后蹲下来，把那天的事一五一十地说了。: James Hao was silent for a long time, then squatted down and told them all of it, everything that had happened that day.
strings.郝建军活着出来了，他的班没有全出来。此后十年，每年清明，他都挨家去送一袋面、一桶: James Hao came out alive; his crew did not all come out. For ten years afterwards, every Qingming Festival, he went from house to house with a sack of flour and a can of oil. He would crouch by the stove without a word, put the things down and leave.
strings.郝建军点了点头，把那一茬炮的事说了出来。说完，他把脸埋进了手里。: James Hao nodded and told them about that last round of shots. When he was done, he buried his face in his hands.
strings.郝建军的管钳和那顶磕瘪了的安全帽，后来交到了他儿子手里。儿子没有下井，考进了县应: James Hao's pipe wrench and his dented hard hat went to his son. The boy never went underground; he passed the exam for the county emergency management bureau and inspects coal mines for a living. The first mine he inspected was Fuyuan.
strings.都往坡下挪，离顶板远一点: Everyone move down the slope. Away from the roof
strings.钱是实打实的；可透水前的事，就永远埋在井下了: The money is real enough. But what happened before the inrush stays buried underground for good
strings.钻孔里吊下来一封信，是矿长亲笔写的：“兄弟们受苦了。出去以后，就说是突然透水、事: A letter came down the borehole, in the mine manager's own hand: “You lads have had it hard. When you get out, say the water came suddenly and there were no signs at all. So long as we all tell the same story, the mine pays every family eight hundred thousand and wages carry on as normal. If anyone talks out of turn, the mine shuts and nobody gets anything.” The letter passed from hand to hand under the cap lamps.
strings.钻孔里吊下来一张名单，让下面的人挨个核对。外包队那一栏写着：“罗国庆，男，二十一: A list came down the borehole for the men to check, name by name. Against the contract crew it read: “George Luo, male, twenty-one”, with a question mark after it. Under it lay a letter marked “For George Luo”, written out at Manny's mother's request. The mine's notice had gone to his cousin's house, and only then did she learn her son was not washing dishes in the county town: “Manny, I don't want money. I only want you out alive.” Manny gripped the letter and could not say a word.
strings.钻孔里吊下来一摞家信。石磊的媳妇写：“孩子会动了，等你回来起名字。”王福山的老伴: A bundle of letters from home came down the borehole. Larry Shi's wife wrote: “The baby's moving. Come back and give him a name.” Felix Wang's wife wrote just one line: “Your dinner's keeping warm in the pot.”—Doug Wei had no letter. He was not on the list up on the surface at all.
strings.钻孔里吊下来第一批东西：几袋葡萄糖水、几盒牛奶，还有医生的字条：“饿久了的人，第: The first things came down the borehole: a few pouches of glucose water, a few cartons of milk, and a note from the doctor: “Men who have gone without food this long get one small pouch each on the first day. Drink it slowly.” But some of them were already wild with hunger.
strings.铁丝碰上电池的那一下，所有人都闭上了眼睛。: The moment the wire touched the battery, everyone shut their eyes.
strings.镐头刨开最后一层砖，一股又冷又呛的气扑了出来，便携仪尖叫个不停。一个满脸煤泥的汉: The pick head broke through the last layer of brick and a cold, choking gas burst out; the detector screamed and would not stop. A man with his face caked in coal slurry rolled out of the hole, his left hand a raw bloody mess, and hit the ground coughing his lungs out: “My name's Charlie Zhao… seven of us in the crew, scattered… my brother's still over there…”
strings.镐尖刨开一层松煤，后面是一道一拃宽的老裂隙，丝丝地往外透着凉气。灰子就是从这儿走: The pick tip broke off a layer of loose coal, and behind it was an old fissure a hand-span wide, breathing out cold air. This is the way Smoky went.
strings.镐把敲在管子上的声音，在巷道里响了一整夜。: The sound of a pick handle on the pipe rang down the roadway all night.
strings.镐把敲在管子上，一下比一下急：三长两短，三长两短。: Pick handle on the pipe, each blow more urgent than the last: three long, two short, three long, two short.
strings.镐把敲在管子上，一声比一声急。: Pick handle on the pipe, each knock more urgent than the last.
strings.镐把敲在管子上：三长两短，三长两短。: Pick handle on the pipe: three long, two short, three long, two short.
strings.问他：你到底多大？: Ask him: how old are you, really?
strings.随它去，别管它: Let it go. Leave it alone
strings.隔壁 1201 老采区运输队的绞车工，在大巷里开了十年绞车，哪儿高哪儿低、哪儿拐: A winch operator from the haulage crew in the old 1201 district next door. Ten years running the winch on the main roadway: where it rises, where it dips, where it bends, he could find with his eyes shut. When the water came, the seven men of his crew were scattered, his younger brother Benny Zhao among them. Right now he is crawling through an old crosscut abandoned years ago, in pitch darkness, inching towards a faint knocking. The winch's wire rope has mangled two fingers on his left hand, and he has been in the water so long that every cough rattles.
strings.韦叔，你莫睡着嘛……你跟我说说话。: Uncle Wei, don't go to sleep… talk to me.
strings.韦德贵又坐了回去，盯着水面，一句话也没说。: Doug Wei sat back down, staring at the water, and said not a word.
strings.韦德贵后来去了哪儿，福源矿上没人说得清。外包队的花名册上，他那一行早就被划掉了。: No one at Fuyuan can say where Doug Wei went. On the contract crew's roster, his line was crossed out long ago.
strings.韦德贵想了半天，只说了一句：“我干的活，不比哪个少。”: Doug Wei thought for a long time and said only: “The work I do is no less than any man's.”
strings.韦德贵把口袋按了按，翻身面朝煤帮躺下了。: Doug Wei pressed his pocket flat, turned over and lay down facing the coal wall.
strings.韦德贵把矿灯绑紧在安全帽上，一步一步走进了水里。: Doug Wei strapped his cap lamp tight to his hard hat and walked into the water, step by step.
strings.韦德贵把饼干掰了一半，放回木板上，一句话也没说。: Doug Wei broke the biscuit in half, put half back on the plank and said nothing.
strings.韦德贵把馒头放在木板上，掰成了好几块。郝建军看了他很久，第一次叫了他的名字：“德: Doug Wei laid the steamed bun on the plank and broke it into several pieces. James Hao looked at him for a long time and used his name for the first time: “Doug.”
strings.韦德贵拿出两个馒头放在木板上，什么也没解释。剩下的，他自己慢慢嚼了。: Doug Wei set two steamed buns on the plank and offered no explanation. The rest he chewed slowly himself.
strings.韦德贵的名字是后来才补进遇难者名单的——一开始，地面上根本不知道井下还有这么一个: Doug Wei's name was added to the list of the dead only later—at first the surface didn't even know there was such a man down there. All he left was an empty bag that had held his bread. The contractor took his ashes back to Guizhou, changing buses three times on the way.
strings.韦德贵盯着坡下的黑水看了很久，突然开口：“这段水，我过得去。”所有人都愣住了。这: Doug Wei stared at the black water below the slope for a long time, then spoke suddenly: “I can get through this stretch of water.” Everyone froze. The contract man—most days he barely said a word.
strings.韦德贵讲完那个小煤窑的事，脱掉了工作服。: When Doug Wei had finished telling them about that little pit, he took off his work clothes.
strings.韦德贵领了一笔比正式工少一截的补偿，又跟着老乡去了内蒙古的一个露天矿。露天的，他: Doug Wei got compensation a notch below a company man's, then followed men from his home county to an opencast mine in Inner Mongolia. Opencast, he said—there's sky over your head.
strings.顶板吱吱作响，煤帮一阵阵往下掉渣，坑木被压得咔咔裂——来压了。老空区渗出的气也多: The roof creaks, the coal walls shed flakes in bursts and the pit props crack under the load—the roof is weighting. More gas is seeping out of the old workings, too.
strings.顶板淋水大了，水顺着锚杆和网片往下滴，在巷道里干活的人很快浑身湿透——接水倒是容: The roof is dripping harder; water runs down the roof bolts and the mesh, and anyone working in the roadway is soon soaked to the skin—though it's easier to catch water now.
strings.顶板还在掉，先退开: The roof's still coming down. Back off first
strings.顶板随时可能再塌: The roof could come down again at any moment
strings.顺着它钻的那道缝往里掏，也许那边透气: Dig in along the crack it squeezed through. Maybe there's air on the other side
strings.顾不上吃的，先把平台垫高: Forget the food—build the platform up first
strings.食物：三个饭盒、半袋饼干和两包方便面，一共约 3500 千卡。坑木树皮的内层有一: Food: three lunch tins, half a bag of biscuits and two packs of instant noodles, about 3,500 kcal in all. The inner bark of the pit props has a little starch in it; sawdust, paper, belts and lumps of coal have almost no calories at all. They only fill the stomach, and they can block the gut or poison you.
strings.饭盒、饼干和水壶被摆在一块平整的木板上。郝建军说：从现在起，谁也不许私自动一口。: The lunch tins, biscuits and water bottles are laid out on a flat plank. James Hao says: from now on, nobody touches a crumb on their own. His own lunch tin, though, is nowhere to be found.
strings.饭盒又被放回了木板上，盖得严严实实。: The lunch tin went back onto the plank, the lid shut tight.
strings.饭盒在每个人手里传了一圈，每人扒了一口。: The lunch tin passed from hand to hand and each man took one mouthful.
strings.饭盒是自己带的，各管各的；没带吃的人就只能分剩下的饼干: You brought your own food, you look after it; anyone who didn't bring any can share what's left of the biscuits
strings.饭盒给了力气最大的人。他埋头吃完，谁也没看。: The lunch tin went to the strongest man. He ate with his head down and looked at no one.
strings.饭盒递到了贺小勇手里。他吃了两口，又推了回来，被王福山硬塞了回去。: The lunch tin was handed to Eddie Ho. He ate two mouthfuls and pushed it back; Felix Wang forced it into his hands again.
strings.饿到第{day}天，胃里像有一把火在烧。有人解下了皮带，泡在水里，放进嘴里慢慢地: By day {day} of hunger, it feels like a fire is burning in your stomach. Someone unbuckles his belt, soaks it in the water and chews it slowly; someone else breaks off a small lump of coal and holds it in his mouth.
strings.黑暗里传来“扑通”一声轻响。: A soft “plop” comes out of the dark.
strings.黑暗里，有人突然喘不上气，心跳得像要炸开，挣扎着要往坡下的水里冲：“我要出去！放: In the dark, someone suddenly can't get his breath, his heart pounding fit to burst, and he struggles to charge down the slope into the water: “I want out! Let me out!”
strings.（“吱”的一声，从小满的手心里叼走了最后一点面渣。）: (With a squeak, it snatches the last flake of noodle from Manny's palm.)
strings.（凑到一只胶靴边上，胡子一抖一抖地闻。）: (Creeps up to a rubber boot, whiskers twitching as it sniffs.)
strings.（咳了半天）……没事，呛了点水，咳出来就好了。: (after a long fit of coughing) …I'm fine. Swallowed some water, that's all. It'll come up.
strings.（喘着气）……便携仪……还有电。我盯着。: (gasping) …the detector… still has charge. I'm watching it.
strings.（趴在最高的那根棚梁上一动不动，肚皮一起一伏，喘得很急。）: (Lies motionless on the highest roof beam, its belly heaving, breathing fast.)
strings.（蹲在压风管口，鼻子冲着管子，一下一下地嗅。）: (Sits at the mouth of the air line, nose to the pipe, sniffing again and again.)
strings.（蹲在饭盒盖上，两只前爪捧着一粒饭渣，啃得飞快。）: (Crouched on a lunch-tin lid, holding a grain of rice in both forepaws, nibbling as fast as it can.)
strings.（黑暗里一阵窸窸窣窣——它又顺着棚梁溜了一圈。）: (A rustle in the dark—it has made another lap along the roof beams.)
